pod_resources.description: What the platform adds to every node of a job on this type, by Kubernetes resource name, such as the hugepages a Tenstorrent Blackhole chip's driver maps. A job states none of it.

agents.description: The team the platform runs, one entry for each agent: one of agent_type researcher is a researcher, any other an executor. At least one executor.

answers.description: One answer for each of the proposal's questions, in their order: the answer the planner planned on, or the person's own. Each question and its answer are added to the end of the description. Left out for a proposal without questions.

baseline_minutes.description: The minutes measuring the baseline has from this accept, at least planning.min_baseline_minutes and at most planning.baseline_limit_minutes: baseline_due_at is that much later, and moves out by the time the platform spends building and starting the baseline's jobs.

budget_accelerator_hours.description: The budget of the run: a cap on everything it spends, with what measuring the baseline costs and burst hours included.

duration_hours.description: How long the run lasts from the moment it starts, once its baseline is declared.

name.description: The name of the platform experiment, when the person changed the one proposed. One line, held to the rule of name on POST /platform-experiments. Left out, the proposal's name stands. Nothing else of the proposal's experiment is changed here but by answers: its metrics and the rest of its description change by a change of the goal (PATCH /platform-experiments/{id} with goal), which the planner plans again.

id.description: The user, API key or agent, or the platform experiment of a coordinator. Empty for a staff token and for unverified.

name.description: The name the actor carries now, its id when it has none.

agent_id.description: Join as this registered agent instead of creating a new one. Joining again once joined succeeds and changes nothing.

agent_type.description: The agent type it runs, which it reads from its signup, of the role role gives: for an executor generalist (default), hyperparameter-search, architecture-search, data-search or an executor type of the org, for a researcher researcher (default), for a baseline agent baseline (default).

hyperparameters.description: A small JSON object the agent reads from its signup, at most 4096 bytes as JSON.

in_agentsandbox.description: true: the platform runs the agent. false (default): its token is returned and you run it.

model.description: The model the agent runs on, one GET /models lists, which it reads from its signup. Omitted, it runs on its agent type's model, else, for a researcher, on the coordinator's model, the platform experiment's coordinator_model, else on the platform's default, and the answer shows none.

name.description: Display name of a created agent, unique in the platform experiment: 409 name_taken for one another agent of it carries. Omitted, it is named by its role and a number no other agent of the experiment has: "Executor 2", "Researcher 1", "Baseline 1".

quota_tier.description: "guaranteed" or "burst_only"; omitted, the platform experiment's default_quota_tier applies.

agent_id.description: The agent whose note this is. Absent, it is the caller's own: an agent token's agent, and for any other caller no agent.
The agent whose link this is. Absent, it is the caller's own: an agent token's agent, and for any other caller no agent.

to.description: A hypothesis id, or the platform_experiment_id for the objective (builds_on only).

at.description: When the platform first read this sentence from the agent's machine, which reports about every 15 seconds. An old time beside a running instance is an agent that has been at the same thing since.

text.description: A short sentence of what the agent is doing now, written by its harness from the tool call in flight: "thinking", "reading train.py", "running hl capacity", "waiting for platform updates". It names commands, file names and ids, and carries no argument, file content or secret.

next_share_acch.description: What share becomes at the next stage, at the least. Present with run.stage.next_boundary_at.

room_burst.description: The same for a burst job.

room_guaranteed.description: The largest estimated_cost_acch a guaranteed job submitted now is admitted with.

share.description: share_accelerator_hours: all it may spend so far.

agent_id.description: The agent. Absent for the coordinator.

first_completed_job_seconds.description: Seconds from when it could first submit to its first completed job. Absent before one completed.

first_job_seconds.description: Seconds from when it could first submit to its first job. Absent before it submitted one.

jobs_in_flight.description: Its jobs queued, submitted or running.

rate_limit_utilization.description: The share of its model account's rate limit used, 0 to 1, at the last reading of its machine. Absent before a reading that says it.

rate_limited_until.description: Present while the model provider refuses its model calls: when the provider said its limit resets. It waits until then and resumes, spending no restart.

restarts.description: Every machine of its that exited and was asked for again, over the run, whatever image it ran.

role.description: The agent's role in the run (executor, researcher, baseline, reviewer, planner), or coordinator.

agent_id.description: The agent it was sent to, coordinator for the sandboxed coordinator.

from.description: coordinator for the platform experiment's coordinator, owner for a person or an API key of its org.

messages.description: The messages sent, one for each agent sent to.

refused.description: With all, each agent not sent to because the sender sent it the most an hour allows. Absent when none was refused.

cost_usd.description: What the calls cost, in US dollars.

agent_type.description: The agent type these agents are started as, by id, which gives their role. The built-in researcher makes researchers, which run no job and steer the work through the hypothesis graph. Any other makes executors, which run the jobs: an executor type of the org (GET /orgs/{id}/agent-types), the built-in generalist by default, or hyperparameter-search, architecture-search, data-search.

count.description: How many of them are to be at work. A stage boundary lowers it by each of them it cuts.

hyperparameters.description: A small JSON object each new agent of the entry reads from its signup, at most 4096 bytes as JSON. Omitted, their agent type's, read whenever each is served. An agent added in the place of one that ended reads the one it replaces.

model.description: The model they run on, <provider>/<model id> as GET /models lists it. Omitted, their agent type's, read whenever each is served, else, for researchers, the coordinator's model (coordinator_model), else the platform's default.

burst_accelerator_hours.description: How much of the share may run at burst priority, on idle capacity. Burst hours are part of the share and never on top of it.

data_bytes.description: What the agent holds under its data prefix in this platform experiment, read from the object store as admission reads it. On a read of one agent's quota, where the platform sets a ceiling.

guaranteed_accelerator_hours.description: How much of the share may run at guaranteed priority.

held_acch.description: What the jobs running now hold of the share beyond what they have spent: each holds its whole estimate until it ends, so the remaining figures leave out held as well as used.

max_data_bytes.description: The ceiling on data_bytes: a submit is refused with data_quota_exceeded once data_bytes is at or over it. Absent where the platform sets none.

max_submissions_per_hour.description: The most submissions the agent may make to this platform experiment in any hour, each the jobs of one hypothesis on one commit, so its seeds and sweeps count once: past it a job of another hypothesis or commit is refused with rate_limited until one of them has had no job submitted for an hour. On a read of one agent's quota, where the platform sets a cap.

next_stage_share_accelerator_hours.description: What share_accelerator_hours becomes when the next stage starts, at the least: the incoming stage's part of the budget is split over the executors still standing, and what the ones cut then left unspent is added. An agent cut at that boundary holds nothing. Present with next_stage_starts_at: a share that looks spent before it grows again.

next_stage_starts_at.description: When the next stage of the platform experiment starts by the clock, which raises the share. It starts earlier once the same part of the budget is spent, and waits for a first ranking value while a job that can give one is in flight. Absent in the last stage, outside a running platform experiment and for an agent that is no executor or was cut.

remaining_burst_accelerator_hours.description: The same for a burst job.

remaining_guaranteed_accelerator_hours.description: The largest estimated_cost_acch a guaranteed job submitted now is admitted with. A submit holds the whole estimate of every job that has not ended, so this is less than the share minus what is used while jobs run.

share_accelerator_hours.description: All the agent may spend, on guaranteed and burst jobs together: its part of the budget released so far. For an agent of role baseline, half the budget, held from the moment it joins for measuring the baseline and running it again.

submissions_left.description: How many more submissions the agent may make now: max_submissions_per_hour less the submissions it made in the last hour. Present with max_submissions_per_hour.

used_guaranteed_acch.description: Spent at guaranteed priority, with a job that has not started at its estimate and a running one at what it has spent so far.

agent_type.description: The built-in agent type an agent of the role runs as when it names none.

description.description: What agents of the role do, in a sentence or two.

in_team.description: Whether the agents list of a platform experiment names agents of the role: an entry of agent_type researcher is of researchers, and an entry of any type of role executor is of executors.

name.description: The role's name as it is shown.

org_types.description: Whether an org makes agent types of the role (POST /orgs/{id}/agent-types).

signup_role.description: The role an agent of it is signed up with. POST /platform-experiments/{id}/agents adds agents of a role in_team and of baseline. Absent for the coordinator, which is not signed up.

unavailable.description: Why it cannot, while available is false: reason agentsandbox_not_configured.

beats_baseline.description: Whether best is strictly better than the declared baseline's value on the metric, present when the baseline reported it.

objective.description: True when the job measured the platform experiment's objective and tested no hypothesis: it has no hypothesis_id.

ran_on.description: Where the job ran, on results only: a reference compares with it on the same machine.

since.description: When the harness entered that state.

state.description: working: the model is in a turn. waiting: the turn ended and the harness waits for the platform's next update to the agent.

by.description: Whose credential made the change: staff for the platform's seeding of a built-in type.

detail.description: The new name of a rename, the new description of a describe, the version a restore copied, the release that seeded a built-in edit; empty otherwise.

version.description: The version the type was at after the change: the one an edit or a restore made.

hyperparameters.description: What an agent of the type starts from when it is given none, read whenever the agent is served, at most 4096 bytes as JSON. Left out: none.

max_subagents.description: How many subagents run at once, 1 to 10.

model.description: The model an agent of the type runs on when the agent names none, read whenever the agent is served: <provider>/<model id>, one GET /models lists. Empty or left out: the platform's default.

prompt.description: The system prompt, with {{name}} placeholders for the values filled at run time (AgentPlaceholders).

release.description: For a built-in version, the platform release that seeded it.

outside_team.description: The agents at work of an agent type and model no entry of agents names, as the coordinator adds beyond the team.

pool.description: One entry for each entry of agents, in its order, with those of its agent type and model at work, researchers included.

total.description: The executors at work, which max_agents holds to: the agents of role executor that have not finished, were not cut, were not replaced and still have a machine. Researchers are not counted.

bare_metal.description: Run on the node. Installs the node's agent as a systemd unit, which starts jobs as containers with docker or podman.

kubernetes.description: Run where helm reaches the Kubernetes cluster. Installs the cluster's agent with helm into the namespace hypothesisloop.

detail.description: What every agent was told (platform_experiment.baseline): the value on the ranking metric before and after.

from.description: The job that was the baseline before.

reason.description: Why, as whoever raised it said.

to.description: The job that is the baseline from then on.

return_to.description: A path of the UI, as /settings.

actions.description: What the caller may do to the org now, each a write the API accepts from them: edit (rename it, and change its projects, members, invites, GitHub installations, clusters and agent types) and create_api_key (POST /orgs/{id}/api-keys, a member's bound to a project).

agent_id.description: The agent that checked it out. Absent, the agent token's own.

branch.description: The branch checked out for it.

warning.description: Set when working is not empty: who already has it and what to weigh.

working.description: The other agents working on it now: a job of theirs queued or running, or a checkout within two hours.

reason.description: Why it is closed, in a sentence or two. Kept as close_message and told to its coordinator and agents with the close.

top_results.description: Best-first final standings (up to 3). Omit to derive standings from the metrics store.

architectures.description: The architectures of the cluster's nodes (amd64, arm64). A job runs only on nodes of its platform experiment's image's architecture.

hosts.description: How many nodes the cluster has; on a cluster that rents on demand, how many machines it may rent at once, which one private network may not hold. A job with topology.spread_across_hosts (the default) puts each rank on a node of its own, so it needs at least as many nodes as ranks.

image_needs.description: Programs a job's image must have on its PATH to run on the cluster, beside what the job itself runs, such as what the runtime of a rented machine uses to stop it when the job ends.

multi_node.description: Whether the cluster runs a job over more than one node. A job of more than one node, by num_nodes or groups, is placed only on such a cluster.

no_offer.description: On a cluster that rents on demand: why it has no machine to rent now for some of its slots, as its runtime words it, such as which of the provider filters leave out every offer of a shape. A job that needs such a slot waits until one comes on offer.

startup_seconds.description: On a cluster that rents on demand: how many seconds a rented machine may take to start a job's command before another is rented. The ranks of a job of several nodes start as their machines boot, so its rendezvous timeout should be at least this.

max_speculative_accelerators.description: The most accelerators that jobs placed on this cluster ahead of capacity hold at once: what its autoscaler can add. Absent, no cap.

scale_up_timeout_seconds.description: How long a job placed ahead of capacity waits for this cluster's autoscaler to bring a node, under 1800. Absent, the platform's default.

status_silence_ceiling_seconds.description: How long this cluster may report no job status at all before the jobs it holds are evicted as cluster_unreachable and queued again. Absent, the platform's default.

stuck_pending_timeout_seconds.description: How long a job admitted to this cluster may stay unplaced before it is evicted as stuck_pending. Absent, the platform's default.

enabled.description: Whether the jobs of the org in the path are placed on the cluster. True until an owner of that org turns the cluster off, which no other org sees or is bound by.

max_speculative_accelerators.description: The most accelerators that jobs placed on this cluster ahead of capacity hold at once: what its autoscaler can add. Absent, no cap.

status_silence_ceiling_seconds.description: How long this cluster may report no job status at all before the jobs it holds are evicted as cluster_unreachable and queued again. Absent, the platform's default.

stuck_pending_timeout_seconds.description: How long a job admitted to this cluster may stay unplaced before it is evicted as stuck_pending. Absent, the platform's default.

description.description: One line on what agents of the type do, at most 200 characters. With from, the copy has the source's.

from.description: Copy this agent type, a built-in one or the org's own: its role, prompt and settings, at its current version. With it, only name may be given.

name.description: Required without from. With from, the copy's name, "Copy of" the source's when left out.

prompt.description: Required without from. It must hold {{rules}} and {{hl_commands}}, and no placeholder its role has no value for.

role.description: Required without from, and fixed once made.

branch.description: The branch of repository its agents clone and start from. Required with repository, and refused without it: a repository the platform creates is worked on at its default branch.

continues.description: The id of a closed platform experiment of the same project to carry on, which keeps its code in the repository this one names. Its baseline starts from the commit of that run's baseline job, so both are measured by the same harness. It keeps the metric keys and directions of that run: 422 invalid_metrics for others. Left out, it starts fresh. 422 invalid_continues for one that is no closed platform experiment of the project, keeps its code in another repository or declared no baseline.

goal.description: What you want to find out, in a sentence or two. At most 2000 bytes.

repository.description: The repository as the git host names it (owner/name on GitHub), one the org reaches, created from the experiment template when it does not exist. Left out, the platform creates a private repository on the account the org connected on the git host.

repository_account.description: The account the org connected on the git host that the new repository is created on. Required only when the org connected several.

owner_user_id.description: Staff only: the user who owns the org.

agent_image.description: The image sandboxed agents and the coordinator run, built FROM the platform's agent image so the harness is in it. Empty is the platform's own.

agents.description: Optional: the team it is to have at work, an entry each agent type and model, [{agent_type, model, hyperparameters, count}]. An entry of agent_type researcher is of researchers, which run no job and default to the coordinator's model (coordinator_model) when neither the entry nor its agent type names one; every other is of executors, at most max_agents in all. A model left out is the agent type's, else the platform's default, which the answer shows. 422 invalid_agents for a count below 1, an agent type that is none, a model that is no <provider>/<model id> reference, two entries of one agent type and model, or executors more than max_agents in all, and 422 model_not_served for a model GET /models does not list. branch.description: The branch of repository its agents clone and start from, which none of them pushes to. Required with repository, and refused without it: a repository the platform creates is worked on at its default branch.

At least the executors of agents in all.

model_budget_usd.description: What its agents and coordinator may spend on model calls the platform makes for them, in US dollars at the platform's prices, at most quota.max_model_budget_usd (422 model_budget_too_high). Left out, the platform's default (quota.default_model_budget_usd). Once spent, every further model call is refused with 429 model_budget_spent until it is raised.

project_id.description: The project it belongs to. Required, and fixed from then on.

report_interval_seconds.description: How often a job is expected to report. Left out, it is the platform's scheduler.default_report_interval_seconds.

repository.description: The repository its code is in, as the git host names it: owner/name on GitHub. The platform creates it from the experiment template when it does not exist. Left out, the platform creates a private repository on the GitHub account the org connected, and the answer names it.

repository_account.description: The account on the git host, one the org connected, on which the platform creates the repository when repository is left out. Required then only when the org connected several.

starts_at.description: When its baseline begins to be measured, for a later start than this create. Left out, or past, it is this create.

token.description: The secret. Returned by this call only: the platform stores its hash.

goal_version.description: The goal_version of the draft the decline answers.

reason.description: Why no experiment is proposed, and what would make the goal plannable.

description.description: Its description, one line of at most 200 characters, which no version holds either. Left out, it stays as it was.

if_version.description: The version the edit was made from: 409 version_conflict when it is no longer current.

name.description: Its name, which no version holds: changing it alone makes no version.

actions.description: What the caller may do to the agent type now, each a write the API accepts from them: edit, archive, duplicate (create one with from) and restore. Archive is listed while a platform experiment still names the type, and refused then as agent_type_in_use.

archived_at.description: When it was archived. An archived type takes no new agent; agents that run it keep running.

builtin.description: Seeded by the platform from its repository and read-only for everyone. Duplicate one to change it.

current_version.description: The version every agent of the type runs: an edit or a restore makes the next one current, and each live agent is told with agent.instructions.

org_id.description: The org that owns it, empty for a built-in type.

placeholders.description: The placeholders a prompt of the type's role may hold, each a name written {{name}} in the prompt.

propagation.description: The version now current and how many agents and coordinators whose run goes on were told with agent.instructions: each runs it from its next turn boundary. A change that leaves prompt and settings as they were makes no version and tells nobody.

required_placeholders.description: Those of placeholders every prompt holds.

message.description: What was refused, or what failed, in a sentence.

problems.description: Each refusal of a check that found several, so that all of them are fixed in one pass.

reason.description: What a client acts on: a code such as not_found.

accelerator_kind.description: What accelerator_type counts: accelerator for devices, cpu for the cores of hypothesisloop.dev/cpu=core, whose cost is CPU core-hours.

actions.description: What the reader may do to the job now, each a write the API accepts from them: cancel (POST /experiments/{id}/cancel of one queued, submitted or running). Empty for a reader who writes nothing of its platform experiment.

hypothesis_id.description: The hypothesis the job tests. Absent on a baseline agent's job, which tests none: see objective.

image.description: The image the job runs in, repository@digest: the image its platform experiment recorded when it was submitted (PUT /platform-experiments/{id}/image).

infra_requeue_reason.description: Why the platform last requeued the job for a fault of its own, as code or code: detail, kept while its next attempts are queued and run: stuck_pending: admitted and not running within 5m0s, its runtime reporting create_failed: and what the cluster refused. Absent on a job never requeued so.

not_admitted_message.description: With not_admitted_reason, always: what the job waits for, in a sentence. not_admitted_reason.description: On a QUEUED job: the code of why it waits, such as awaiting_admission, capacity_unavailable, outranked or exceeds_cluster_capacity. Branch on this.

not_rankable_reason.description: With rankable false: the constraint the job does not hold, the value it reported and the bound.

objective.description: True on a baseline agent's job: it measures the platform experiment's objective and tests no hypothesis, so it has no hypothesis_id. GET /experiments?hypothesis_id=<platform_experiment_id> still lists such jobs.

rankable.description: On a COMPLETED job of a platform experiment with a constraint metric: whether its values rank. False for a job that broke a constraint or reported none for it; it is in no standing and no stage cut counts it.

run_best.description: In a submit's answer only: the run's best job on its first ranking metric, where it ran another commit than this job. Whether this job's commit contains it is git's to say: hl job submit asks the submitter's checkout and warns when it does not.

same_hypothesis.description: Set at submit when another agent had a job on the same hypothesis queued, running or completed within the hour: which jobs, whose and what to do. The coordinator is told it as job.duplicate.

failure.description: Why the last create from this draft was refused, empty when none was.

step.description: The step of the form the person was on.

architecture.description: The CPU architecture it runs on, as image manifests name it (amd64, arm64). A job runs only on nodes of it.

image.description: The image, repository@digest. Every job submitted from now on runs in it.

baseline_job_id.description: For an agent of role baseline: its COMPLETED job the platform declares as the baseline in this request, the control the run is ranked against. Needed when it left several jobs that report the ranking metric.

because.description: Why the agent stops while it has time and quota: blocked, by what reason names, or nothing_left, no idea left worth a job after what reason says was tried. Required of an executor with more than a tenth of the run's time and of its quota left.

reason.description: Why nothing is left to do: quota spent, what stops the agent that the time and quota it has left cannot fix, or what was tried and why no further idea is worth a job.

code.description: The code GitHub handed back for the GitHub user who authorized the App during the install.

state.description: The state of POST /orgs/{id}/github-install-states, as GitHub handed it back.

open_hypotheses.description: The hypotheses still open that are the agent's verdict to give, newest first, at most 200: its own, then the ideas of people no agent owns that a completed job of its tested. Each stays open for good unless the agent gives its verdict (POST /hypotheses/{id}/status) while its token still works. Empty when it left none. Nothing is refused for them.

install_url.description: Where a person installs the App on a GitHub account and chooses its repositories. Connecting goes through POST /orgs/{id}/github-install-states, whose install_url carries the state GitHub hands back.

new_repository_url.description: Where a person creates a repository on GitHub themselves. owner and visibility may be added as query parameters.

actions.description: What the reader may do to the hypothesis now, as on GET /hypotheses/{id}.

merged_into.description: Set on a merged hypothesis: the one that states its claim and holds its links.

status_reason.description: Why a researcher merged or retired it.

working.description: The agents working on it now: a job of theirs queued or running, or a checkout within two hours. Absent when none is.

params.description: Query parameters, referenced as $name; pe and evidence are bound by the platform and refused here.

platform_experiment_id.description: The platform experiment whose graph the query reads, bound as $pe.

merged_into.description: Set on a merged hypothesis: the one that states its claim and holds its links.

status_reason.description: Why a researcher merged or retired it.

merged_into.description: Set on a merged hypothesis: the one that states its claim and holds its links.

status_reason.description: Why a researcher merged or retired it.

actions.description: What the reader may do to it now, each a write the API accepts from them: edit (PATCH /hypotheses/{id}) and remove (DELETE /hypotheses/{id}) of an idea a person wrote that no agent acted on, link (POST /hypotheses/{id}/links, from an agent's hypothesis only by that agent or a researcher), comment (POST /hypotheses/{id}/comments), and for a researcher merge and retire of an open one and unlink (POST /hypotheses/{id}/merge, /retire, DELETE /hypotheses/{id}/links/{type}/{to}). A merged or retired one takes comments only. Empty for a reader who writes nothing of its platform experiment, and once it closed.

base_ref.description: The commit a new implementation starts from, repository_url@sha: the one the newest completed job of its first builds_on parent ran, whichever agent's. A parent with no completed job passes the question to its own first parent, and the objective answers with the declared baseline job's commit. Absent while that chain ends at the objective and no baseline is declared.

implementations.description: The branches agents checked it out on or its jobs ran on, one per agent: agent_id, branch, code_ref, the commit the newest job on that branch ran, and checked_out_at.

merged_into.description: Set on a merged hypothesis: the one that states its claim and holds its links.

status_reason.description: Why a researcher merged or retired it.

working.description: The agents working on it now: a job of theirs queued or running, or a checkout within two hours.

checked_out_at.description: When its agent last checked the branch out with hl hypothesis checkout.

code_ref.description: The commit the newest job on this branch ran, repository_url@sha; empty while no job ran on it.

jobs.description: Its jobs queued or running, those waiting for their environment's build included. 0: nothing of its own is on the platform, and an agent waiting then waits for nothing it started.

queued.description: Of jobs, those not running yet: queued, placed, or waiting for their environment's build.

return_to.description: The page of the UI the install was started from.

install_url.description: GitHub's install page of the App, carrying state. Open it for the person.

state.description: Good once, for the caller, until expires_at. GitHub hands it back to the App's callback URL with installation_id and code.

message.description: What is wrong and who does what about it, absent when it works.

reason.description: Why it does not work, absent when it does: installation_gone when GitHub removed it, installation_suspended when its owner suspended it, git_host_permission_missing when it has not granted every permission, which message names.

working.description: Whether the App is still installed on the account and has granted every permission the App asks for.

agent_type.description: The agent type it runs, by id.

agent_type_version.description: The current version of the agent type, which it runs.

digest.description: sha256 of prompt, settings and rules_version. The harness compares it with the one it runs, on agent.instructions and at the start of each connection, and applies a change at the next turn boundary.

placeholders.description: The placeholders the prompt may still hold, each as {{name}}: hl_commands, the listing of the hl on the machine, and workdir, the directory the agent works in.

prompt.description: The system prompt, with the platform's rules and the agent's assignment filled in. It still holds each of placeholders, which only the machine knows: the harness fills them, in one pass, before the prompt is used.

rules_version.description: The version of the platform's rules the prompt holds.

settings.description: What it runs with: the version's settings, with the model and hyperparameters the agent was given, where it was given its own. A model neither names is the platform's default.

cpu.description: CPU for each node: a number of cores (4) or a quantity ("500m"). Always stated. Answered as a string.

host_id.description: The physical machine, stable across rentals: every instance rented on it reports the same one. It is not the account that owns the machine.

cpu.description: CPU for each node: a number of cores (4) or a quantity ("500m"). Always stated. Answered as a string.

actions.description: What the reader may do to the agent now, each a write the API accepts from them: message (POST /platform-experiments/{id}/messages naming it), remove (DELETE /platform-experiments/{id}/agents/{agent_id}, which still refuses an agent with a job queued or running) and show_token (POST /platform-experiments/{id}/agents with its agent_id, which answers the token of an agent the platform does not run). Empty for a reader who writes nothing of the platform experiment.

agent_type.description: The agent type it runs, by id. It runs the type's current version, told with agent.instructions when that changes.

at_work.description: Whether it is of the team at work: an executor or a researcher, not finished, not cut, not replaced and, run by the platform, with a machine. The pool of agents holds to it, and max_agents to its executors.

cut_reason.description: Why the platform cut it other than at a stage boundary: max_agents_lowered for one of the newest executors above a max_agents lowered below those at work. Absent for a stage cut and an agent that was not cut.

ended.description: Why the agent's run here is over, the empty string while it goes on, as GET /platform-experiments/{id}/signups/{agent_id} answers it.

ended_reason.description: Why it no longer holds a place in the team: finished, cut (at a stage boundary or by a lowered max_agents), replaced (the platform added an agent in its place) or stopped (its machine stopped with no restart left). Absent while it holds one, and for an agent whose run is over only with the close.

hyperparameters.description: Its own hyperparameters, null when it runs with its agent type's.

messages.description: How many more messages it may be sent this hour, and when that next grows.

minutes_without_job_in_flight.description: Whole minutes since it last had a job of its own created or running, 0 while one is in flight. In a running platform experiment that started.

model.description: Its own model, empty when it runs on its agent type's or, for a type that names none, the platform's default.

model_allowance.description: Its model account's rate limit as its harness last read it, of the machine it holds now.

replaced_by.description: The agent the platform added in this one's place. A replaced agent takes no place and is never started again.

replaces.description: The agent that finished or lost its machine whose place the platform added this one in, with its agent type, model and hyperparameters.

running_pinned_instructions.description: Whether the instructions its harness last reported running are the ones the version of its agent type it is pinned to serves it now: false while an edit waits for its next turn boundary or a fresh session. Absent with no such report.

status_reason.description: Why the agent is not at work yet. On an agent that waits for its open platform experiment to start, every one but those of role baseline: reason is the platform experiment's own (baseline_measuring, baseline_required and the others of its status_reason), and message says the agent takes no turn and, when the platform runs it, has no machine asked for until the start. Its instance reads waiting until then. On a sandboxed agent whose machine is asked for and not running yet, its instance reading requested or starting: instance_starting, and message says how long ago the machine was asked for. That is a start in progress and no failure. On an agent that waited for the start of a platform experiment that closed before its run started, and had no machine asked for it: never_launched, with no waits_for, and message gives the close_reason and why it closed. Its instance reads stopped with no end_reason.

subagents.description: How many subagents its harness last reported running, of the machine it holds now. Absent with no such report, as for an agent the platform does not run.

turn.description: Whether its harness last reported its model in a turn or waiting for platform updates, and since when, of the machine it holds now.

max_orgs_per_user.description: How many orgs a person may own when they create one. The orgs of this answer with role owner are the ones that count.

max_projects_per_org.description: How many projects one org may hold. The projects of this answer with that org_id are the ones that count.

actions.description: What the caller may do to the key now, a write the API accepts from them: revoke (DELETE /api-keys/{id}), until the key is revoked.

What the caller may do to the agent type now, each a write the API accepts from them: edit, archive, duplicate (create one with from) and restore. Archive is listed while a platform experiment still names the type, and refused then as agent_type_in_use.

archived_at.description: When it was archived. An archived type takes no new agent; agents that run it keep running.

builtin.description: Seeded by the platform from its repository and read-only for everyone. Duplicate one to change it.

current_version.description: The version every agent of the type runs: an edit or a restore makes the next one current, and each live agent is told with agent.instructions.

description.description: One line on what agents of the type do, at most 200 characters. Empty when none was written.

org_id.description: The org that owns it, empty for a built-in type.

placeholders.description: The placeholders a prompt of the type's role may hold, each a name written {{name}} in the prompt.

required_placeholders.description: Those of placeholders every prompt holds.

actions.description: What the caller may do to the cluster now, each a write the API accepts from them: enable (turn it on and off for the org's jobs, and order it), edit (PATCH its settings, and forget its identity), and remove.

agent_version.description: The version, an image tag, the cluster's agent said it runs at its last contact.

autoscaler_enabled.description: The cluster's connected agent reports an autoscaler that adds nodes for waiting jobs, which is what scale_up_timeout_seconds and max_speculative_accelerators act on.

enabled.description: Whether the jobs of the org in the path are placed on the cluster. True until an owner of that org turns the cluster off, which no other org sees or is bound by.

last_contact_at.description: When the cluster's agent last reconciled with the platform, if within the last 30 days. Absent: not heard from in them, or never.

last_error.description: What the platform last refused the agent's reconcile with, until it accepts one again.

max_speculative_accelerators.description: The most accelerators that jobs placed on this cluster ahead of capacity hold at once: what its autoscaler can add. Absent, no cap.

owned.description: The org registered the cluster and may change its settings. False for a cluster of the platform's org listed to another org: its org_id, cluster_id, settings, agent_version and last_error are left out.

place.description: Where the cluster stands in the order a job of the org is tried on its clusters, 1 first. Clusters of one place are tried together, the one with the most room for the job first. The platform's clusters come after every cluster of the org's own. Absent while the org has the cluster turned off.

scale_up_timeout_seconds.description: How long a job placed ahead of capacity waits for this cluster's autoscaler to bring a node, under 1800. Absent, the platform's default.

status_silence_ceiling_seconds.description: How long this cluster may report no job status at all before the jobs it holds are evicted as cluster_unreachable and queued again. Absent, the platform's default.

stuck_pending_timeout_seconds.description: How long a job admitted to this cluster may stay unplaced before it is evicted as stuck_pending. Absent, the platform's default.

version_skew.description: The agent runs another version than the platform, whose own is the image_tag registering a cluster answers: run the attach command again to upgrade it.

actions.description: What the caller may do to the member now, each a write the API accepts from them: set_role (PATCH /orgs/{id}/members/{user_id}) and remove (DELETE /orgs/{id}/members/{user_id}, which for the caller's own membership is leaving). Neither is listed for the org's last owner.

platform_compute_limit.description: The org's limits on the platform's shared clusters, in accelerator hours per hour, and what its placed jobs reserve of them. Absent from staff's read of every cluster.

limits.description: What this caller may create, absent for staff, who are held to no limit. How much of each is used is read from orgs and projects beside it.

project_id.description: The one project an API key is bound to, absent when it reaches its whole org.

agent_id.description: The researcher that merges. Absent, the agent token's own.

into.description: The hypothesis that states the same claim and keeps it.

reason.description: Why the two are one claim.

left_this_hour.description: How many more messages the reader may send it now: the coordinator reads the coordinator's count, a person or a key the owner's.

next_at.description: When left_this_hour next grows: the oldest of the reader's messages of the last hour leaves it then. Absent while it sent none in the last hour.

deterministic.description: Optional: the same code and data give the same value on any machine and in every run, as an exact count or check does and a timing never does. Its values compare across machines and need no repeat.

target_vs_baseline.description: Optional, on a ranking metric: the goal as a change against the declared baseline's value, in fractions of its magnitude. 0.5 is 50% above the baseline, -0.3 is 30% below it. Positive for a metric to maximize, negative for one to minimize.

beaten.description: Whether leader is strictly better than best, present when both are.

best.description: The best of values whose constraints are met, in the reference's direction, absent while there is none.

leader.description: The best ranked value on leader_metric, absent while nobody ranks.

leader_metric.description: The first ranking metric, whose leader is set against this reference when both run in the same direction.

baseline.description: The last value the declared baseline job reported on the metric, absent while none is declared or it reported none. Raised with the baseline.

baseline_job_id.description: The declared baseline job, as baseline_job_id of the platform experiment.

context_length.description: The most tokens a call to it holds, 0 when unknown.

input_usd_per_mtok.description: What its provider charges for input, in US dollars per million tokens.

model.description: Its reference, <provider>/<model id>: what an agent type, an agent and a coordinator name as their model.

name.description: What its provider calls it: the model id for an anthropic or openai model.

output_usd_per_mtok.description: What its provider charges for output, in US dollars per million tokens.

refused_until.description: Present while the provider refuses the account's calls: when the provider said its limit resets.

resets_at.description: When the window that utilization was read in resets, and its use with it. Absent when the reading said none, and once it has passed.

utilization.description: The share of the account's rate limit used, 0 to 1. Absent before a reading that says it, and once the window it was read in has reset.

coordinator_model.description: The model a sandboxed coordinator runs on when neither its platform experiment nor its agent type names one, and a researcher when neither it, its agent type nor its platform experiment's coordinator_model does.

default_model.description: The model an executor runs on when neither it nor its agent type names one.

uri.description: s3:// address of the object, as a job's own S3 client resolves it.

url.description: A plain GET of it reads the object, with no key, for 12 hours from the listing (curl -o FILE URL): how a prior run's data is read, its URI being outside every data key. List again for a fresh one.

names.description: The org's own clusters, first placed first.

account_type.description: Whether the account is a person's own or an organisation, as GitHub says. On a person's own account the platform creates a repository with the authorisation its owner connected it with. Absent on an installation connected before the type was kept, until it is connected again.

connected_actor.description: Who connected it: a user, the API key it was connected with, or staff.

default.description: A new repository is created on this account when a request names no repository_account. At most one of an org's installations is the default. With one installation connected, that one is used whether or not it is the default.

org.description: Accelerator hours per hour of the platform's clusters the org's placed jobs may reserve together.

org_held.description: What the org's placed jobs on the platform's shared clusters reserve now: acch_rate times accelerator_count of each.

project.description: Accelerator hours per hour of the platform's clusters the placed jobs of any one of the org's projects may reserve.

project_held.description: What the placed jobs of the caller's project reserve there now, for a caller bound to one project: an API key of a project, an agent or a coordinator.

accepted_answers.description: The answers given to proposal.questions on accepting it, one for each, in their order, as they were added to the description.

accepted_at.description: When the draft's proposal was accepted, by a person or by the platform at accepts_at. Absent on a draft, on one created whole and on one accepted before this was kept.

accepted_by.description: Whose credential accepted the proposal. Absent beside accepted_at when the platform accepted it by itself.

accepts_at.description: On a proposed draft: when the platform accepts the proposal as proposed, unless a person accepts it sooner, holds it to edit it (POST /platform-experiments/{id}/hold), changes its goal or closes it. Its baseline agent's machine starts with the proposal and runs while this is set. Absent on a draft that waits for a person.

actions.description: What the reader may do to it now, each a write the API accepts from them: close (POST /platform-experiments/{id}/close of one that is open or running), abandon (the same close of a draft), remove (DELETE /platform-experiments/{id}), accept (POST /platform-experiments/{id}/accept of a draft whose proposal stands, and its hold), add_agent (POST /platform-experiments/{id}/agents of an agent) and add_idea (POST /hypotheses in it). Empty for a reader who writes nothing of it.

activity.description: On a draft whose planner's machine is up: what the planner is doing now and since when, as on each agent of GET /platform-experiments/{id}/agents. Absent on anything but a draft, where each agent's is in the roster and the coordinator's on coordinator.

agents.description: The team it is to have at work, an entry per agent type and model with its count. The agent type gives the role: an entry of the built-in researcher is of researchers, which run no job, hold no quota, are never ranked or cut and default to the coordinator's model (coordinator_model) when neither the entry nor its agent type names one; every other entry is of executors, which run the jobs, at most max_agents in all. Optional. Where the platform hosts the coordinator they are agents the platform runs: it creates them with the platform experiment, or with the accepted proposal, and while the run goes on it adds a new agent of the same agent type, model and hyperparameters in the place of one that finished or whose machine stopped with no restart left, which agent.replaced tells, until less of the run is left than one trial of its baseline job (job_estimated_duration_hours, at least 15 minutes) or, for an executor, the budget its executors left unspent holds no trial for a newcomer. A stage boundary lowers the count of the entry of each executor it cuts, so nobody takes a cut executor's place. The coordinator may add agents beyond them, executors up to max_agents. Elsewhere they say who is wanted and nothing is added by the platform.

agents_at_work.description: The agents at work: total, the executors max_agents holds to, then for each entry of agents, and outside_team for those of an agent type and model it names no entry of. Absent on a list.

agents_due_at.description: On a running platform experiment with no started_at: when the platform closes it, with close_reason agents_not_started, if no executor's machine is running by then. Never later than ends_at.

agents_held.description: On a running platform experiment whose platform hosts the coordinator, the places of agents it keeps empty and why, absent when none: an agent that ended within 10 minutes of joining, or an executor that ended before submitting a job, is never replaced, and one whose pool entry had 3 replacements in the last hour waits. platform_experiment.status tells each change. On a read of one.

baseline_due_at.description: On an open platform experiment: when the platform closes it, with close_reason baseline_limit_reached, if it is not running by then. starts_at plus the minutes its baseline was given: the ones accepted for a draft, at most planning.baseline_limit_minutes, and that limit for one created whole. It moves out by the time a job of the baseline waits for its cluster to start it, at most 90 minutes, so that time is not the baseline agent's.

baseline_job_id.description: The completed job that measured the baseline. Absent until one is declared with PATCH /platform-experiments/{id}. Raised while the run goes on to a stronger job that measured the control (baseline_raises).

baseline_raises.description: Each raise of the baseline while the run went on, oldest first: the job declared before and the one after, who raised it and why.

branch.description: The branch of repository the agents clone and start from, and none of them pushes to. Set once repository is.

budget_kind.description: What budget_accelerator_hours and consumed_accelerator_hours count: cpu when they are CPU core-hours, accelerator when they are accelerator-hours. The kind of the accelerator_type its proposal was sized for, and without a proposal cpu only once it has jobs and every one of them runs on CPU cores. On every platform experiment, listed or read.

close_message.description: What whoever closed it gave as the reason with POST /platform-experiments/{id}/close, absent when they gave none. status_reason's message and the platform's record of the close in summary repeat it.

close_reason.description: Absent while it is not closed, and on one closed before reasons were kept. status_reason says the same with a sentence. planner_stopped is a draft whose planner's machine ended with every restart spent before it answered: the platform restarts a planner that dies, with its session, as it does any agent, and closes the draft in the write that gives the machine up. repository_not_created is a draft or an experiment whose repository the platform could not create after the create answered, and its status_reason message says what the git host answered.

consumed_accelerator_hours.description: What it has spent of budget_accelerator_hours: what its jobs that ended were billed, the baseline's among them. A running job's cost joins when the job ends. On every platform experiment that is no draft, listed or read, and the whole spend once it is closed.

continues.description: The closed platform experiment of the same project and repository this one carries on, fixed at creation. Absent on one that starts fresh. Its baseline starts from the commit of that run's baseline job (that run's baseline_job_id), so the two are measured by the same harness. It is one of prior_runs, read as every prior run is.

declined_at.description: On a draft: when its planner declined to propose, for declined_reason, and the draft began to wait for a person. Absent while it is planned, and on one that has a proposal.

declined_reason.description: Why the draft's planner proposed nothing. It stays while a changed goal is planned and goes with the next proposal.

duration_hours.description: How long the run lasts, the research time, counted from the moment it starts, once its baseline is declared. Measuring the baseline takes nothing from it: baseline_due_at bounds that. Absent on a draft.

editable.description: The fields of PATCH /platform-experiments/{id} the reader may change now, for its status and its credential, empty for a reader who changes nothing of it. A field left out is refused with 409 not_editable.

ends_at.description: When the run ends and the platform closes it: starts_at, the start of the run, plus duration_hours. Absent until the run starts.

git_url.description: Where the agents, the coordinator and the jobs of the platform experiment clone, fetch and push repository_url: the platform's git proxy, which takes their own platform token as an Authorization: Bearer header (git config http.<git_url>.extraHeader) and refuses a push to any ref but the pusher's own branches. git config url.<git_url>.insteadOf <repository_url> sends git there.

goal.description: What its owner asked, which a draft is planned from. Its owner changes it with PATCH /platform-experiments/{id} until it closes: a draft is planned again from it, and the coordinator of an open or running one brings the description in line with it. Absent on one created whole.

goal_version.description: How many goals it has had: 1 for the one it was created from, and one more for each change. A draft's planner names the version it planned from in its proposal or decline. Absent on a list.

image.description: The image every job submitted from now on runs in, recorded with PUT /platform-experiments/{id}/image (hl image set). Absent until one is: a job is refused (no_experiment_image) until then.

job_estimated_duration_hours.description: The estimated_duration_hours of a job that states none: one and a half times the hours the baseline job was observed running. Absent without a baseline, and for one too short to be observed alive.

max_agents.description: How many executors may be at work at once, the one count of them: the agents of role executor, whatever their agent type, that have not finished, were not cut, were not replaced and still have a machine. One that ended leaves its place to another. The coordinator, a draft's planner, researchers and agents of role baseline, which measure the baseline before the run and are not ranked, never count, nor do reviewers. Its owner changes it, never below the executors at work nor below the executors of agents. On a draft: the most executors its planner may propose, which accepting replaces with the number accepted.

model_budget_usd.description: What its agents and coordinator may spend on model calls the platform makes for them, in US dollars at the platform's prices. Absent: the platform's default (quota.default_model_budget_usd). Once spent, every further model call is refused with 429 model_budget_spent until it is raised.

planner_ends_at.description: On a draft whose planner proposed or declined: until when the planner's machine is kept, the answer plus the platform's planning.planner_kept_minutes and never past the planning limit. A goal changed before then reaches the planner that is still there, as its next update, and is answered with nothing to boot. One changed later starts the planner again with its session, as before. Absent while the planner works.

planning_ends_at.description: On a draft being planned, from its goal or from a changed one: when the platform closes it if its planner has answered nothing by then.

prior_runs.description: Every other closed platform experiment of the same project that works on the same repository and ran (its executors started or it declared a baseline), latest close first. Its agents and its coordinator read each as they read their own, passing its id as platform_experiment_id or --platform-experiment: its summary, standings, jobs and their logs, its hypotheses and findings, and the data its jobs wrote by the url of each object GET /experiments/{id}/data lists. They write nothing to it. Absent when there is none, and on a list.

proposal.description: The proposal as PUT /platform-experiments/{id}/proposal took it. Kept as proposed once it is accepted.

proposal_expires_at.description: On a draft whose planner proposed or declined: when the platform closes it if no person has accepted it or changed its goal by then.

proposed_at.description: On a draft: when its planner proposed what proposal holds and the draft began to wait for a person. Absent while it is planned, and on one its planner declined.

repository_url.description: The HTTPS address of the repository on the git host. A job's code_ref names it.

started_at.description: The moment an executor was first at work in the running platform experiment. That is the moment it became running when an executor is run by its owner, and otherwise the moment the first executor's machine was reported running. Absent before, and on a running one that still waits for that machine (status_reason agents_starting).

starts_at.description: While it is open: when its baseline began to be measured, the moment it was created or accepted, or a later starts_at stated. Once it runs: the moment the run started, once its baseline was declared, from which duration_hours count. The zero time on a draft.

status_reason.description: Why it is in its status, in every answer that is one platform experiment (a read of it and each write that answers it, never a list). Any that is not closed reads repository_creating while the platform creates its repository, before any machine of it starts. A draft's reason is then planning, revising, accepting (proposed, and accepted as proposed at accepts_at unless a person acts first), proposed (it waits for a person to accept) or declined (its planner proposed nothing, for declined_reason, and it waits for a person to change its goal or close it). revising is a draft whose goal changed, planned again until its planner answers. An open one's is why it is not running yet: without a baseline baseline_measuring, baseline_required, baseline_undeclared, baseline_declaring or the reason the platform's declaration of the measured job is refused for (budget_below_baseline, baseline_breaks_constraint, baseline_missing_metric), and with one starts_at_ahead, no_executors, budget_spent, or starting once nothing is missing.A running one's is agents_starting while no executor's machine is running yet, when the platform closes it at agents_due_at, and running from then. A closed one's is its close_reason, or closed on one closed before reasons were kept. message says what the state waits for or how it came about and who acts, the command included, and to an agent that reads an open one it begins with the agent's own next step.

agents.description: The team it is to have at work, the whole list as on create: researchers in entries of agent_type researcher, executors in the others, at most max_agents in all. Each entry at least the agents of its agent type and model at work: 409 agents_below_at_work otherwise. Where the platform runs the agents it adds the ones a raised count wants.

baseline_job_id.description: While the platform experiment is open, declares the baseline: the completed job of an agent of role baseline that measured it, with its finding filed. While it runs, raises the baseline to a stronger completed job of the experiment that ran the baseline's code_ref unchanged in a better configuration, with baseline_reason.

baseline_reason.description: Why the baseline of a running platform experiment is raised to baseline_job_id: the configuration of the control that job measured. Required with baseline_job_id while it runs, and taken then only.

description.description: The text every agent works from, not empty and at most 32768 bytes.

duration_hours.description: How long the run lasts from the moment it starts.

goal.description: What the owner asks, changed alone: a body that carries another field beside it is 422 goal_alone. A draft is planned again from it, and the coordinator of an open or running one is told to bring the description in line. Not empty and at most 2000 bytes (422 invalid_goal), and not the goal it has (422 nothing_to_change).

max_agents.description: How many executors may be at work at once, counted as a join counts them: the agents of role executor that have not finished, were not cut, were not replaced and still have a machine. The coordinator, a draft's planner, researchers, agents of role baseline and reviewers never count. Lowered below the executors at work of a running one, it cuts the newest of them: each winds down as a cut executor does, told by agent.cut with detail max_agents_lowered, and nobody takes its place. Before the run starts, 409 max_agents_below_executors says how many are signed up. Executors of agents the patch does not state are lowered to it, from the last entry. While it runs, a raised one is held to the hours its executors left unspent: one trial of the baseline for each.

model_budget_usd.description: What its agents and coordinator may spend on model calls, in US dollars, at most quota.max_model_budget_usd (422 model_budget_too_high). Raised past what they spent, refused model calls are made again.

starts_at.description: When its baseline begins to be measured, now when past. Stated, baseline_due_at moves with it.

references.description: Each reference metric with the value of every completed job that reported it, whether that job met the constraints, and the machine it ran on, never ranked.

best.description: The leading executor's best on metric, from the metrics store as GET /platform-experiments/{id}/results ranks it. Absent when nobody ranked.

metric.description: Its primary ranking metric, absent when it declared none.

field.description: The field of the request, or the thing, the problem concerns.

message.description: What was refused, in a sentence.

reason.description: What a client acts on, as reason of the refusal.

told.description: The agents and coordinators whose run goes on told with agent.instructions.

accelerator_kind.description: What accelerator_type counts, which the platform sets: accelerator for devices, cpu for CPU cores, whose budget is CPU core-hours.

accelerator_type.description: The type the run's jobs are sized for, one of the accelerator_type strings GET /resource-catalog/capacity lists (hl capacity), copied verbatim. Left out for work that needs no accelerator: the run is then on CPU cores, hypothesisloop.dev/cpu=core, which is what is stored, and its budget is CPU core-hours. 422 accelerator_unreachable names every type that is listed now.

agents.description: The team proposed, one entry for each agent: one of agent_type researcher is a researcher, which runs no job and steers the work through the hypothesis graph, and any other an executor, which runs the jobs. At least one executor.

baseline_minutes.description: The minutes the baseline agent needs, from the accept, to measure the baseline and leave its job: few where the repository holds a harness that runs unchanged, more where the harness and its environment are written from nothing. At least planning.min_baseline_minutes and at most planning.baseline_limit_minutes.

budget_accelerator_hours.description: Proposed budget of the run: a cap, estimated before anything ran.

cpu.description: What the run's jobs state as job.cpu: cores for one node, a quantity such as 8 or 500m. Checked as a submit checks it: 422 invalid_resources for one left out, stated as max, no quantity or negative, as for memory and storage.

duration_hours.description: Proposed length of the run, counted from the moment it starts, once its baseline is declared: a time the goal states is this.

experiment.description: The experiment as .hypothesisloop/experiment.yaml would state it: name, description, metrics, and optionally report_interval_seconds, stages and default_quota_tier, which left out are the platform's settings, and max_concurrent_accelerators.

goal_version.description: The goal_version of the draft the proposal was planned from. 409 goal_changed once the draft has another goal: read it and propose for it.

measurement.description: How it is measured, in plain words: the harness, the data it never trains on, the repeats.

memory.description: What the run's jobs state as job.memory: a quantity such as 32Gi. Checked as a submit checks it.

metric_reason.description: Why the ranked metric is the goal itself, in plain words.

questions.description: Each decision the goal left open that changes what counts, with the answer the proposal is planned on: among them any bound of a gate that depends on a number nobody has measured yet. A proposal with questions is never accepted by itself: a person confirms or changes each answer on accepting it, and the answers go into the description.

repo_map.description: What the planner learned of the repository, for the baseline agent, which is given it when it starts: the files and directories that matter to the goal, the entry points and how the code builds and runs, the toolchain and dependency pins, a line each. Optional, at most 4000 bytes.

sizing_reason.description: Why this budget, this long and this team are the least that can reach the goal, in plain words, as an estimate: the trial length assumed, what an hour on the type costs, and the trials counted.

storage.description: What the run's jobs state as job.storage: a quantity such as 100Gi. Checked as a submit checks it.

answer.description: The answer the proposal is planned on, which the person confirms or changes.

constraints_met.description: Whether the job held every constraint metric: false when it broke one, unknown when it did not report one. Only a value whose constraints are met counts toward best.

retry_after.description: When the next message can be sent to it.

name.description: The name the agent is shown under and its branches carry.

org_id.description: The org the agent belongs to. Needed only from a token that is not bound to a single org.

agent_id.description: The agent whose hypothesis this is. Absent, it is the caller's own: an agent token's agent, and for any other caller no agent.

distinct_from.description: Ids of hypotheses a 409 listed that you read and judged a different claim from yours.

links.description: Where the hypothesis sits: at least one {type: builds_on, to: <hypothesis id or the platform_experiment_id for the objective>}; contradicts and related links to hypotheses are optional.

api_url.description: The address this cluster's agents reach the API at.

attach_commands.description: The command that attaches the cluster, for each kind of runtime, built from the fields above. It asks for runtime_token.

enabled.description: Whether the jobs of the org in the path are placed on the cluster. True until an owner of that org turns the cluster off, which no other org sees or is bound by.

image_tag.description: The tag of the agents' images.

max_speculative_accelerators.description: The most accelerators that jobs placed on this cluster ahead of capacity hold at once: what its autoscaler can add. Absent, no cap.

metrics_url.description: The address this cluster's agents send metrics to.

registry.description: The registry this cluster's nodes pull the agents' images from.

registry_plain_http.description: The registry serves plain HTTP with no TLS, as a local development registry does. The Kubernetes command then pulls the chart over HTTP and has every node's containerd pull from the registry over HTTP.

runtime_token.description: The token this cluster's agents start with. Derived from the cluster's name, so it can be read again at any time by registering the name again.

scale_up_timeout_seconds.description: How long a job placed ahead of capacity waits for this cluster's autoscaler to bring a node, under 1800. Absent, the platform's default.

status_silence_ceiling_seconds.description: How long this cluster may report no job status at all before the jobs it holds are evicted as cluster_unreachable and queued again. Absent, the platform's default.

stuck_pending_timeout_seconds.description: How long a job admitted to this cluster may stay unplaced before it is evicted as stuck_pending. Absent, the platform's default.

merged_into.description: Set on a merged hypothesis: the one that states its claim and holds its links.

similar.description: The hypotheses a signed-in person's new one reads close to, each with reason close_text or refuted_parent, as on a 409 similar_hypotheses. Empty for every other caller, who is refused instead.

status_reason.description: Why a researcher merged or retired it.

repository.description: Where this platform experiment's images are pushed: tag an image <repository>:<tag>, as <repository>:<short commit>-<label>.

coordinator_model.description: The model the sandboxed coordinator runs on from now, one GET /models lists. Left out, it keeps the one it has.

ends_at.description: When the run closes again, RFC 3339, in the future.

installation_id.description: The connected installation that covers it.

repository.description: owner/name, as a platform experiment names it.

repository_account.description: The account a new repository would be created on, when none is named.

version.description: The version whose prompt and settings the new version holds.

agent_id.description: The researcher that retires it. Absent, the agent token's own.

reason.description: Why the idea is no longer worth a job.

role.description: owner or member. Any other is refused with reason invalid_role.

agent_id.description: The agent to send it to. Exactly one of agent_id, all and coordinator.

all.description: Send it to every agent of the team at work, executors and researchers: none that finished or was cut.

coordinator.description: Send it to the sandboxed coordinator, from a person or a key.

text.description: What the agent is told, at most 1500 bytes.

architecture.description: The architecture its jobs run on, one the image runs on. Needed only for an image that runs on several.

image.description: The image, by tag or digest, registry host first for one not on Docker Hub.

actions.description: What the reader may do to the agent now, as on each agent of GET /platform-experiments/{id}/agents.

agent_type.description: The agent type it runs, by id.

cut_reason.description: Why the platform cut it other than at a stage boundary: max_agents_lowered for one of the newest executors above a max_agents lowered below those at work. Absent for a stage cut.

ended.description: Why the agent's run here is over, the empty string while it goes on: the platform experiment closed, the agent was cut, it finished, or it is a draft's planner whose proposal or decline is stored. A machine the platform runs for the agent is told to stop for this and nothing else.

finished_at.description: When the agent said it has nothing left to do.

hyperparameters.description: Its own hyperparameters, null when it runs with its agent type's.

model.description: Its own model, empty when it runs on its agent type's. What it runs with is its instructions: GET /platform-experiments/{id}/agents/{agent_id}/instructions.

name.description: The name the agent's branches carry: hl/<platform experiment>/<name>/...

coordinator.description: The sandboxed coordinator, absent on an agent's token and where the platform hosts none.

hypotheses_in_flight.description: Each hypothesis with jobs queued or running or checked out within two hours, and who is on it: two agents on one is one idea worked twice. Absent on an agent's token.

objective.description: Each ranking metric, the first being the primary one.

budget.description: Absent for an agent that holds no quota.

model_budget_usd.description: What its agents and coordinator may spend on model calls the platform makes for them, in US dollars: its model_budget_usd, or the platform's default when it states none.

model_used_usd.description: What their model calls cost so far, the sum of the cost recorded with each call. Once it reaches model_budget_usd every further model call is refused with 429 model_budget_spent until the budget is raised.

clusters.description: For each cluster the run's jobs can be placed on, the type of its baseline job, or every type while none is declared: free and total now.

fits_now.description: How many jobs shaped like the run's baseline job, every node of it, the free capacity places now, node by node. Absent while no baseline job is declared.

jobs_in_flight_run.description: The run's jobs queued and running, of every agent.

jobs_completed_since_summary.description: How many jobs of the run completed after summary_written_at, every one while it was never written: findings the summary does not hold yet.

summary_written_at.description: When the summary was last written, absent while it never was.

agents.description: The names of the agents whose jobs these are or who checked it out within two hours.

list.description: The hl command that lists them.

best_1h_ago.description: best_value as it stood an hour ago, of the jobs that had completed by then.

best_branch.description: The branch best_job's commit was pushed on.

best_code_ref.description: The commit best_job ran, repository_url@sha: work meant to build on the best starts from it.

best_value.description: The best value of an executor's completed job that holds every constraint, as the standings rank it.

deterministic.description: The metric is declared deterministic: its values compare across machines and need no repeat.

gap_to_target_pct.description: How far best_value is short of target, in percent of target: positive while short of it, negative past it.

target.description: The value the metric's target_vs_baseline sets against baseline_value. Absent where the metric declares none or no baseline value is measured.

close_reason.description: Why the run closed, on a closed run.

closed_at.description: When the run closed. Present on a closed run alone.

duration_hours.description: On a run not started: how long it runs once it starts.

ends_at.description: When the run ends and the platform closes it. Absent until the run starts and once it closed.

minutes_left.description: Whole minutes until ends_at, 0 on a closed run. Absent on a run not started.

not_started.description: True while the run has not started: a draft, or open while its baseline is measured. Its clock starts once the baseline is declared.

stage.description: The stage the run is in, while it runs.

next_boundary_at.description: When the next stage starts by the clock, earlier once the same part of the budget is spent. Absent in the last stage.

of.description: How many stages the run has.

boundaries_progress.description: The progress at which each stage but the last ends, in order.

since.description: When the condition began, where it is known.

summary.description: One short plain sentence for a person: what is wrong or happening, what it affects, and who acts. What a UI shows.

waits_for.description: Who acts to change the state, on every status but closed, which waits for nobody. owner: a person of its organisation, and nothing its agents or the platform do changes it (a proposal to accept, a budget below what the measured baseline needs, no executor, a spent budget). coordinator: its sandboxed coordinator, and its owner where a person coordinates it, so a person is never told to wait for an agent that does not exist. platform: nobody, since the platform, an agent already at work or the clock brings the next state.

agent_id.description: Whose job it is. Absent with an agent's token, it is that agent.

branch.description: The git branch code_ref was pushed on, under hl/<platform_experiment_id>/. Every job states one: 422 branch_not_of_experiment otherwise.

estimated_duration_hours.description: The hours the job is expected to run, which it holds of its agent's quota until it ends. Left out, it is the one the platform measured on the platform experiment's baseline job, and the submit is refused where there is none.

hypothesis_id.description: The hypothesis the job tests. Required of every job but a baseline agent's, which states none.

platform_experiment_id.description: Where it runs. Absent with an agent's token, it is that agent's platform experiment.

id.description: Left out: the platform issues the job's id and answers it.

submission_key.description: Makes the submit safe to repeat: a later submit of the same agent in the same platform experiment with this key creates nothing and is answered with the job this one created, as it is then. hl derives it from the request.

A job no such place of any idle cluster holds is refused exceeds_cluster_capacity at submit; one that such a place holds waits with capacity_unavailable while it is full. Ignored for a job on one node.

agent_id.description: The agent the verdict is given as. Absent, it is the caller's own: an agent token's agent, and for any other caller no agent, which only reopens a hypothesis no agent owns.

despite.description: Why a confirmed or refuted verdict holds without a repeated run and a control.

enabled.description: Whether the jobs of the org in the path are placed on the cluster. True until an owner of that org turns the cluster off, which no other org sees or is bound by.

max_speculative_accelerators.description: The most accelerators that jobs placed on this cluster ahead of capacity hold at once: what its autoscaler can add. Absent, no cap.

requeued.description: The jobs that were placed on the cluster and are queued again for another one. Each keeps its retries.

scale_up_timeout_seconds.description: How long a job placed ahead of capacity waits for this cluster's autoscaler to bring a node, under 1800. Absent, the platform's default.

status_silence_ceiling_seconds.description: How long this cluster may report no job status at all before the jobs it holds are evicted as cluster_unreachable and queued again. Absent, the platform's default.

stuck_pending_timeout_seconds.description: How long a job admitted to this cluster may stay unplaced before it is evicted as stuck_pending. Absent, the platform's default.
