post.description: Submit {metadata, job}. The platform issues the job's id, job-<32 hex>, and answers it as id. AcceleratorType/count are derived from the job spec. submission_key makes the submit safe to repeat when its answer was lost: a second submit of the same agent with the same key creates nothing, holds nothing more of the quota and is answered 202 with the job the first created, as it is then, so its status may no longer be QUEUED. The key is the caller's to choose and to change when it means another job. metadata.agent_id is whose job it is and whose quota it spends, and metadata.platform_experiment_id where it runs. An agent's token says both: it may leave them out, and stating another is refused. Who submitted it is the caller, answered as actor. metadata.estimated_duration_hours is what the job holds of its agent's quota until it ends, answered on the job as it was applied. A stated one is never replaced; left out, it is the platform experiment's job_estimated_duration_hours, which the platform measured on its baseline job, and 422 required where it measured none. Nothing is measured before the job of an agent of role baseline: left out there, it is the largest that agent's quota admits now, within the stage's per-job limit and the time left until baseline_due_at, and what the job does not spend is given back when it ends. metadata.code_ref is the platform experiment's repository at a commit, repository_url@<40-character sha>, with no credential in it: 422 code_ref_not_in_repository for any other address. metadata.branch is the git branch that commit was pushed on, one agent's implementation of the hypothesis, under hl/<platform_experiment_id>/: 422 branch_not_of_experiment for any other. What ran is code_ref, and the branch says which line of work it belongs to. The job runs in the image its platform experiment records at the submit (PUT /platform-experiments/{id}/image), answered on the job as image, repository@digest, and only on nodes of that image's architecture: 422 no_experiment_image while none is recorded. job.command, or each group's, is required, 422 malformed: every node fetches the job's commit into /workspace/code and runs the command there. 422 researcher_submits_no_job for an agent of role researcher, which runs no job. 422 experiment_not_started before the platform starts the run, when only the job of an agent of role baseline is accepted: on an open platform experiment the message is its status_reason, the reason and the caller's own next step as GET /platform-experiments/{id} words them. job.cpu, job.memory and job.storage, or each group's, are what one node of the job holds, each stated as a quantity (cpu: 2, memory: 8Gi, storage: 4Gi): 422 required, naming the field in problems, where one is left out or is max. A job holds what it states and nothing is sized from the node it lands on. 422 exceeds_cluster_capacity where the job asks for more than every cluster that runs it has with nothing else on it, with what it asks for and what each cluster has: no wait admits such a job. A cluster that scales up may yet hold it. One that reports nothing now is named and not judged, and where none is judged the job is queued. 422 no_cluster_for_architecture where the job's image runs on an architecture no node of the clusters that run it has, naming the image's architecture and the ones those clusters have: a cluster that scales up may yet add a node of it. 422 exceeds_project_compute_limit where the job alone reserves more accelerator hours per hour of the platform's clusters than its project may hold (GET /resource-catalog/capacity, platform_compute_limit) and no cluster of the org's own can hold it. metadata.hypothesis_id and metadata.theory are required of every job but that of an agent of role baseline. The baseline is the objective's own measurement: that job states neither, 422 baseline_tests_no_hypothesis when it names a hypothesis, its branch is hl/<platform_experiment_id>/baseline, and it is answered with objective true and no hypothesis_id: it belongs to the objective, which is no hypothesis to look up. Any agent may run its own implementation of any hypothesis of the platform experiment, whoever registered it. same_hypothesis on the answer names the jobs of other agents that test the same hypothesis, queued, running or completed within the hour: the job is queued all the same, and whoever steers the run is told it as job.duplicate. run_best on the answer names the run's best job on the first ranking metric, its value, commit and branch, where it ran another commit than this job: whether this job's commit contains it is git's to say, which hl job submit asks the submitter's checkout. The job is queued all the same. Two fields have a default, answered on the job as applied: metadata.capacity_tier left out is guaranteed, and job.max_retries left out is 0. 503 object_store_unavailable while the platform's object store does not answer: a submit measures the agent's durable data there and creates the job's data key in it, so nothing was stored and the same submit is repeated later. Rejections return {reason,message}; an accepted job remains QUEUED until current capacity fits. Every not_admitted_reason comes with its sentence in not_admitted_message.
post.summary: Submit one job

get.description: Whole-set totals for the same ?agent/?platform_experiment_id/?hypothesis_id/?project_id/?status/?since/?search filters GET /experiments accepts, counted in PostgreSQL. Every list read is bounded to one page, so this is the only way to get a total that is not the page's own length -- ask this before listing anything. evictions_by_reason is the cheapest diagnosis you have: several jobs evicted 'silent' or 'never_reported_metrics' means your reporting path is broken, not that training is slow, and resubmitting unchanged fails the same way. evictions_by_class folds the same tally into whose fault it was: 'workload' is yours, 'infrastructure' is the environment's (those cost you no quota and no retry attempt -- stop debugging code that was correct), and 'policy' is the platform's own decision, such as a stage cut, which is not a failure at all. in_flight_accelerators sums accelerator_count over SUBMITTED and RUNNING jobs on an accelerator type, and in_flight_cores does so for jobs on CPU cores. ?group_by=agent or ?group_by=hypothesis adds groups: the same counts once per agent or hypothesis that has a matching experiment, keyed by its id.

post.description: Every hypothesis has a place in its platform experiment's graph: links needs at least one {type: builds_on, to} where to is an existing hypothesis id, or the platform_experiment_id itself for the objective. Several builds_on make a combination of ideas; contradicts and related links may be added too. Find where your idea belongs first with POST /hypotheses/query. Idempotent within a platform_experiment_id: text equivalent to an existing hypothesis (modulo case/whitespace) returns that row with 200 and already_existed=true and your links are not applied; a new one returns 201. While the text reads close to hypotheses of the platform experiment it does not build on (word overlap, at a lower bar for one that builds on the objective alone), or a builds_on target is refuted, it answers 409 similar_hypotheses with each of them in problems, its id the field, and registers nothing until each is named in distinct_from or in a contradicts or related link. A signed-in person is not refused: their hypothesis is registered with 201 and the ones it reads close to come back in similar, as a hint. The returned id is metadata.hypothesis_id for the job testing it; every job must reference a hypothesis from its own platform experiment. Who registered it is the caller, answered as actor, and no field of the body names it: author is refused. agent_id says whose hypothesis it is: an agent token's is its own agent's, named or not, and any other caller names an agent it reaches to register for it, or names none and the hypothesis has no owning agent. Both sit in the same graph under the same dedup, and any agent may submit a job against either. 403 not_signed_up for an agent that has no place in this platform experiment. 403 baseline_registers_no_hypothesis for an agent of role baseline: the baseline is the objective's own measurement and its job names no hypothesis. 409 experiment_closed once the platform experiment is closed, for every caller. What one with no owning agent does not get is quota or a place in the standings — those key on agent_id.

post.description: Read-only Cypher against one platform experiment's hypothesis graph (Memgraph). Body {platform_experiment_id, cypher, params}; answer {columns, rows, truncated}. Use it to find where an idea belongs before registering it, and to walk lineage. Schema: (:Objective {id}) is the root of one platform experiment, id = platform_experiment_id. (:Hypothesis {id, platform_experiment_id, agent_id, actor_kind, actor_id, text, status, created_at, status_changed_at, status_actor_kind, status_actor_id}). agent_id is whose hypothesis it is, empty on one no agent owns. actor_kind (user, key, agent, coordinator, staff) and actor_id are the credential that registered it, and status_actor_* the one that gave the verdict; a node from before they were kept has neither, and author holds the name it stated. created_at and status_changed_at are datetimes, returned as RFC3339 text: compare them with datetime('2026-10-02T01:30:00Z'), since a string never matches one. Relationships, each {agent_id, actor_kind, actor_id, created_at}: (:Hypothesis)-[:BUILDS_ON]->(:Hypothesis or :Objective) (refines, extends, combines; acyclic, every hypothesis has one or more), (:Hypothesis)-[:CONTRADICTS]->(:Hypothesis), (:Hypothesis)-[:RELATED]->(:Hypothesis). A query reads this platform experiment and nothing else, whatever it returns: the platform rewrites it before it runs. Every node pattern names its label, (h:Hypothesis) or (o:Objective), and is tied to $pe (platform_experiment_id on a hypothesis, id on the objective), which you may leave out or write as {platform_experiment_id: $pe} and {id: $pe}; a variable-length relationship ([:BUILDS_ON*1..3]) stays inside the platform experiment and takes no filter of its own; a text search keeps this platform experiment's hits. Refused with 422 naming cypher: a node without a label, as (n), () or a variable in parentheses on its own, which is then written (n:Hypothesis) again, another or a second label, the scope property set to anything but $pe, a parameter as a property map, a function outside the built-in ones (count, sum, avg, min, max, collect, coalesce, exists, all, any, none, single, reduce, extract, size, length, head, last, tail, range, reverse, isempty, id, labels, type, properties, keys, nodes, relationships, startnode, endnode, degree, indegree, outdegree, tostring, tointeger, tofloat, toboolean, tolower, toupper, trim, ltrim, rtrim, replace, split, substring, left, right, startswith, endswith, contains, abs, ceil, floor, round, sqrt, sign, exp, log, log2, log10, datetime, date, localtime, localdatetime, duration, timestamp), a statement that does not start with MATCH, OPTIONAL MATCH, WITH, UNWIND, RETURN or CALL, and a CALL without YIELD node. $evidence is bound to a map by hypothesis id of what is outside the graph: {jobs (rejected aside), submitted, queued, running, completed, failed, evicted, rejected, findings, comments} as counts and last_finding_at (datetime). A hypothesis with none of these has no entry and reads as null: `WHERE coalesce($evidence[h.id].jobs, 0) = 0` finds the untested ones. $evidence[$pe] is the objective's: the baseline's jobs and the comments on the objective. Full-text index hypothesis_text over Hypothesis.text, ranked by how many of your words match: `CALL text_search.search_all('hypothesis_text', 'warmup cosine schedule') YIELD node, score RETURN node.id, node.text, node.status, score ORDER BY score DESC LIMIT 10` (plain words; quotes, colons and parentheses are search syntax). Children of a hypothesis: `MATCH (c:Hypothesis)-[:BUILDS_ON]->(:Hypothesis {id: $id}) RETURN c.id, c.text, c.status`. Nodes come back as their properties plus _labels, relationships as properties plus _type, _from and _to, paths as lists. Nothing a query writes persists (writes go through POST /hypotheses and POST /hypotheses/{id}/links). LOAD CSV, periodic commits and procedures other than text_search.search, text_search.search_all, text_search.regex_search, text_search.fuzzy_phrase_search are refused. Limits: 5s and 256 MB of memory per query, 200 rows (truncated=true when cut). A Cypher error comes back as 422 naming cypher, with Memgraph's message. Findings, comments and jobs are not in the graph: GET /hypotheses/{id} returns them, and GET /hypotheses/{platform_experiment_id}/comments the objective's comments.

post.description: open (default) / confirmed (validated as a real improvement) / refuted (confidently established as not working) / inconclusive (noisy or not worth drilling into). Every verdict but open needs a job of the hypothesis that completed or failed, else 409; despite never replaces it. confirmed and refuted are given with the evidence: against names the control, a completed job of the same platform experiment, and the hypothesis has two completed jobs of its own besides it, or one where every ranking metric of the platform experiment is declared deterministic. Without that the answer is 409 with what is missing, unless despite carries a sentence of why the verdict holds anyway: a repeat is needed only where results vary between runs. Where every ranking metric is declared deterministic and the hypothesis has a completed job of its own, the control is named and despite stands in for nothing (409). A control that holds is the basis even with despite beside it. What a verdict rests on is kept as a comment on the hypothesis. Only the agent whose hypothesis it is may set it; anyone else gets 403. A hypothesis no agent owns, a person's or a researcher's idea, is settled by an agent that ran a job of its own on it that completed or failed, else 403 verdict_needs_own_job; with no agent named it is only reopened (open), as the coordinator does. A researcher gives no verdict: 403 researcher_gives_no_verdict. agent_id says as which agent the verdict is given: an agent token's is its own, named or not, and any other caller names the owning agent, or the agent that tested one no agent owns, to rule for it. Who gave it is the caller, answered as status_actor. 409 hypothesis_merged or hypothesis_retired for a merged or retired one, which takes no verdict. 409 experiment_closed once the platform experiment is closed, for every caller.

Only the org's administrators edit: a member is refused with 403, and so is anyone editing a built-in type (builtin_read_only), which only the platform's repository changes. 409 version_conflict when if_version is not current, archived for an archived type; 422 invalid_agent_type for a prompt or settings an agent could not run with, model_not_served for a model GET /models does not list; 429 rate_limited once 60 versions of the type were made in the last hour.
put.summary: Make the next version of an org's agent type

post.description: An archived type takes no new agent and is no longer edited; nothing is deleted. 409 agent_type_in_use while a platform experiment that is not closed names it, in its agents, for its coordinator or for one of its agents. Only the org's administrators archive, and nobody a built-in type.
post.summary: Archive an org's agent type

get.description: The newest first: who created, edited, renamed, described, archived or restored it, when, and the version it was at after. Nothing is ever removed from it.
get.summary: List every change of an agent type

post.description: Inserts the next version with the prompt and settings of version, makes it current and tells every agent and coordinator of the type whose run goes on with agent.instructions, as an edit does. Restoring what the current version holds makes no version. Name and description stay as they are. Only the org's administrators restore, and nobody a built-in type (builtin_read_only). 404 for a version the type does not have, 409 archived for an archived type, 429 rate_limited as for an edit.
post.summary: Make an earlier version of an org's agent type current again

get.description: The newest first. A version is never changed: each edit made the next one.
get.summary: List every version of an agent type

get.description: Newest first, revoked ones included. No token is ever listed. Every member sees them all. An API key sees itself and the keys minted from it.
get.summary: List an org's API keys

post.description: Returns the token once: the platform keeps its hash only, so a lost token is replaced by a new key. It is the one secret of this API that cannot be read again; a cluster's runtime token and an agent's token are derived and are returned whenever asked. With project_id the key reaches that project only, without it the whole org. An owner creates either; a member one bound to a project. A key works while the person who created it could still create it: it stops when they leave the org, and one of the whole org when they stop being an owner. A key may mint keys no wider than itself, and revoking a key revokes every key minted from it.
post.summary: Create an API key

get.description: The clusters the org registered and the platform's, which serve every org, in the order a job is placed on them, with whether an agent is connected right now and whether the org has the cluster on for its jobs (enabled). The org may change only the ones it owns, and turns any of them off or on for its own jobs.
get.summary: List the clusters an org's jobs run on

post.description: A cluster exists for the platform once its name is registered, and takes the jobs of its org only, or of every org for a cluster of the platform's org. Returns what its agents are started with: the runtime token, the two addresses they reach the platform at, and attach_commands, the complete command that starts them on a Kubernetes cluster and on a bare-metal node. The token is derived from the name, so it is never lost: registering a name the org already owns changes nothing and returns the same token and addresses. A name another org owns answers 409.
post.summary: Register a cluster for an org

put.description: names is every cluster the org registered, each once, first placed first: anything else answers 422 and changes nothing. A job is placed on the first cluster that can take it as the scheduler reads capacity at that moment, and on a later one when that is full or has just failed it. The order holds for placements from then on and moves no job that is placed. A cluster registered afterwards comes last until it is ordered, and the platform's clusters come after every one of the org's own. Answers the clusters as the list does, in the new order.
put.summary: Set the order an org's jobs are placed on its clusters

delete.description: Ends the cluster for the platform. Every job placed on it goes back to the queue in the same step, keeping its retries, and is placed on another cluster that takes its org. The cluster's settings and the identity bound to it are deleted, and its runtime token is refused from then on, so stop its agents. The name is free to register again, by any org. requeued names the jobs.
delete.summary: Remove a cluster from an org

patch.description: Takes the fields that change, at least one. scale_up_timeout_seconds, max_speculative_accelerators and stuck_pending_timeout_seconds are the cluster's own values in place of the scheduler's defaults, for a cluster whose nodes appear when a job asks for them, and status_silence_ceiling_seconds how long the cluster may report no job status before the jobs it holds are evicted as cluster_unreachable: each takes a value, or 0 to go back to the default.

post.description: From here on no job of the org is placed on the cluster, and the capacity the org reads leaves it out. The org's jobs already placed there are not touched: they run to their end. A queued job of an org that turned off every cluster it could use waits with not_admitted_reason clusters_disabled. The cluster is any the org can use, its own or one of the platform's, and the decision is the org's alone: it changes nothing for another org. An owner of the org, an API key of the whole org and staff decide it. Repeating it changes nothing. A cluster the org cannot use is not found.
post.summary: Turn a cluster off for an org's jobs

post.description: The org's jobs are placed on the cluster again, which is how every cluster starts. The cluster is any the org can use, its own or one of the platform's, and the decision is the org's alone: it changes nothing for another org. An owner of the org, an API key of the whole org and staff decide it. Repeating it changes nothing. A cluster the org cannot use is not found.
post.summary: Turn a cluster on again for an org's jobs

delete.description: A cluster is bound to the first cluster_id its runtime reports, and a runtime reporting any other is refused. After the machines behind a name are rebuilt they report a new one: forget the old identity here and the cluster binds to what its runtime reports next. The cluster keeps its name, priority and settings.
delete.summary: Forget the identity a cluster's runtime reported

post.description: For an owner of the org, as a user or an API key. Answers a state good once, for the caller, for 15 minutes, and install_url, GitHub's install page of the App carrying it. The person installs the App there on their own GitHub account or an organisation, or changes the repositories of an installation they made before. GitHub has them authorize the App and sends them to the App's callback URL with state, code, installation_id and setup_action, and POST /github/installations connects the installation. return_to is the page of the UI the install starts from, handed back when it finishes. 422 invalid_request when it is not a path of the UI. 503 github_not_configured.

post.description: Operator/dashboard endpoint. project_id, name, description, metrics, budget_accelerator_hours, max_agents and duration_hours are required. max_agents is how many executors (agents of role executor, whatever their agent type) may be at work at once, and counts nobody else: no researcher, no agent of role baseline, which measures the baseline before the run, no reviewer, no coordinator and no planner. agents, optional, is the team the run starts with and is to keep at work: an entry each agent type and model with its count, [{agent_type, model, hyperparameters, count}]. The agent type gives the role (GET /agent-roles): an entry of the built-in researcher is of researchers, which run no job, hold no quota, are never ranked or cut, count toward no max_agents and default to the coordinator's model (coordinator_model) when neither the entry nor its agent type names one; every other entry is of executors, which implement and run the experiments, at most max_agents in all. duration_hours is how long the run lasts from the moment it starts, at most the platform's quota.max_platform_experiment_days (422 invalid_length without it, run_too_long over that). The answer carries no ends_at: the run ends duration_hours after it starts. Created, it is open until its baseline is declared and the platform starts the run, and baseline_due_at in the answer is until when: planning.baseline_limit_minutes after starts_at, which is this create or a later one the body states. One not running by then is closed with close_reason baseline_limit_reached. Three fields left out are the platform's settings: report_interval_seconds is scheduler.default_report_interval_seconds, stages is stages.default, as one stage of its whole length when max_agents is below 5, since a boundary cuts nobody from fewer executors (more than one stage stated for such a field is refused invalid_stages), and default_quota_tier, which controls signups that omit quota_tier, is quota.default_quota_tier. The platform starts the run, and nothing else does: once a baseline is declared (PATCH baseline_job_id), at starts_at or at once without one or with one past. Until then it is open and GET /platform-experiments/{id} says in status_reason what it waits for. What it is created as is checked by the rules a draft's proposal is checked by, and refused with 422 and the same reasons: invalid_experiment, invalid_metrics, invalid_stages, invalid_cost, invalid_agents, invalid_length, run_too_long, and accelerator_unreachable when no cluster the org's jobs can be placed on reports capacity now (GET /resource-catalog/capacity lists none): nothing of it could run. coordinator_in_agentsandbox: true has the platform run the coordinator as one more machine beside the agents', on coordinator_model or the platform's coordinator default: it holds this platform experiment's coordinator token, is no agent of it, holds no quota and is not ranked. The coordinator's machine is asked for once the plan is accepted and the experiment is open, so it supervises the baseline and can change the lineup before the start, and is kept until the experiment closes. It is fixed from then on. repository is the code the platform experiment works on, named as the git host names it (owner/name on GitHub): agents clone it and push their branches to it, jobs check it out, and repository_url in the answer is where from. branch, required with repository, is the branch the agents clone and start from and none of them pushes to: 422 invalid_branch for one git takes no name of or one under hl/, branch_not_found for one the repository does not have. A repository named that the org cannot reach is created from the experiment template (git_host.experiment_template_repository) before anything else, as POST /projects/{id}/repositories does: its default branch holds one commit of the template's files. Left out, the platform creates a private one on the account the org connected on the git host, named from the experiment and its id and generated from the experiment template, after the create answered: the answer has no repository yet and status_reason repository_creating, no machine of it starts before the repository is recorded, and a read then names it in repository, repository_url and branch, its default branch. branch is refused without repository (422 invalid_request). On GitHub, the installation covers a repository it created whichever repositories its owner selected. With several accounts connected, repository_account says which, and 422 repository_account_required lists them when it is left out; it is never stated with repository (422 invalid_request). 422 git_host_not_connected when the org has connected no account on the git host, and installation_not_connected when repository_account is none it connected: those are answered before anything is created. When the git host does not create it (the authorisation is gone, the host refuses the creation, the name is taken), the platform experiment is closed with close_reason repository_not_created, and its status_reason message carries what the git host answered. A repository the request names is never written to. Named on GitHub, an installation of the platform's GitHub App that the org connected must cover the account that owns it (GET /orgs/{id}/github-repositories lists what may be named): 422 invalid_repository when it is not owner/name, installation_not_connected when the org connected no installation on the account that owns it, repository_not_reachable when it exists and the installation does not cover it, and installation_gone when the App was removed on GitHub. 502 git_host_failed when the git host answers 5xx or not at all, the message naming what it was asked for and its answer. On a deployment whose git host is plain, repository is a name under the host's root, created there from the template when it does not exist, and is required: 422 repository_required without it. agent_image is the image the sandboxed agents and the coordinator run, built FROM the platform's agent image so the harness is in it. Left out, it is the platform's own. 422 invalid_agent_image when it is no image reference. Both are fixed from then on. With coordinator_in_agentsandbox: true it also creates, in the same write, one sandboxed agent for each place of agents, of its entry's agent type, role, model and hyperparameters, whose machines are asked for when the run starts. While the run goes on the platform keeps them at work: it adds a new agent in the place of one that finished or whose machine stopped with no restart left, with its agent type, model and hyperparameters, until less of the run is left than one trial of the baseline job (job_estimated_duration_hours, at least 15 minutes) or, for an executor, the budget its executors left unspent holds no trial for one, and a stage boundary lowers the counts by the executors it cuts, so none of them is replaced. agent.replaced tells each agent added. It also creates one sandboxed agent of role baseline, named by its role, as accepting a draft does: its machine is asked for at once, it measures the baseline, and the platform declares the job it leaves when it finishes, so status_reason reads baseline_measuring from the first answer and nobody adds a baseline agent. 409 max_agentsandboxes_reached where the platform's limit holds no machine for it beside the coordinator's. Without coordinator_in_agentsandbox this call creates the experiment and no agent, and the platform adds none: every executor and researcher, and any other agent, joins by its own POST /platform-experiments/{id}/agents. max_agentsandboxes in the answer is how many machines the platform runs for this platform experiment at once, its sandboxed agents of every role and its coordinator together: one of them is kept for an agent of role baseline, and an agent that finished holds none. GET /platform-experiments/{id} shows the coordinator's model and what became of its machine.
post.summary: Create a platform experiment

post.description: Creates a platform experiment in status draft from goal, one sentence saying what the caller wants to find out. A draft has no budget, no metrics, and one agent, its planner, which the platform runs (role planner, in the roster like any agent) and nobody else joins: the planner works out how to measure the goal and proposes the metrics, the description, the hardware, the budget and the agents, and it opens only when that proposal is accepted: by a person, or by the platform as proposed at accepts_at. Until then its max_agents is the most agents a proposal's team may name: max_agentsandboxes less the coordinator and the baseline agent an accepted draft is given. A draft takes no job, so nothing is measured and no compute is spent until then. Its name is the goal cut short until the proposal names it. POST /platform-experiments creates one whole instead, and states what a run costs itself. Closing a draft (POST /platform-experiments/{id}/close) abandons it. Its planner and later its agents keep their code in repository: the one the request names, checked as on POST /platform-experiments, or a private one the platform creates on the account the org connected on the git host. repository_account says which account when the org connected several. 422 git_host_not_connected, repository_account_required and installation_not_connected as on POST /platform-experiments. A repository the platform creates is created after this answers: the draft is answered without repository and with status_reason repository_creating, and its planner starts once the repository is there. When the git host does not create it the draft is closed with close_reason repository_not_created, and its status_reason message says what the git host answered. repository and branch are checked as on POST /platform-experiments, and a repository named that does not exist is created from the experiment template. On a deployment whose git host is plain, repository is a name under the host's root and is required: 422 repository_required without it. 422 invalid_goal for a goal that is empty or over the length, invalid_continues for a continues that names no closed platform experiment of the project and repository with a declared baseline. 503 agentsandbox_not_configured when the deployment has no sandbox provider to run the planner on.
post.summary: Start planning a platform experiment from one sentence

delete.description: Takes the platform experiment off the platform for every account: its lists, its reads and those of everything in it, its hypotheses, jobs, standings and watch stream, answer 404 from then on, to staff too, and the tokens of its agents and coordinator are refused. Whoever may close it removes it. One not closed yet is closed first as POST /platform-experiments/{id}/close closes it, every running job evicted and every agent stopped, with close_reason removed, in the same write. Nothing it holds is deleted, and what it spent counts toward every total as before. Its agents and its coordinator are told with platform_experiment.removed. 404 for one removed before.

get.description: Returns status, budget, the stage ladder, the list of signed-up agents and prior_runs, the closed runs of the same project and repository that its agents and coordinator read as their own. consumed_accelerator_hours is what it has spent of its budget, the whole spend once it is closed. status_reason says why it is in its status, in every status. duration_hours count from the moment the run starts, which a running one holds in starts_at, and ends_at is that start plus duration_hours. A running one reads agents_starting while no executor's machine is running yet: the first one that is sets started_at, and the platform closes it at agents_due_at (close_reason agents_not_started) when none comes up. From then it reads running, and executors_done once every executor has finished, was cut or lost its machine with no restart left: nobody is left to submit a job, the platform still closes it only at ends_at, and waits_for names who writes the summary and closes it before, its coordinator where the platform hosts one and its owner otherwise. A closed one reads its close_reason. An open one says why it is not running yet. Without a baseline that is where the measuring stands: baseline_measuring (an agent of role baseline is at work, and the platform declares its job when it finishes), baseline_required (none is at work and none left a job to declare: one is added), baseline_undeclared (they left several jobs and one is declared with PATCH), baseline_declaring (the platform is about to declare the one job), or what the platform's declaration of that one job is refused for, by the reasons of PATCH baseline_job_id: budget_below_baseline, baseline_breaks_constraint, baseline_missing_metric. With a baseline: starts_at_ahead, no_executors, budget_spent, or starting when nothing is missing: the request that declares the baseline or adds the executor starts the run itself. The message says what the state waits for and who acts, with the hl command, and to an agent it begins with that agent's own next step: an agent of role baseline is told to measure, and any other that its jobs are refused until the start. Nothing else says what an open platform experiment waits for.repository is the code it works on, as the git host names it, and repository_url the address agents clone and jobs check out. Both are absent when it names none. One made from a sentence carries goal and goal_version, and while it is a draft what its planner proposed (proposal, proposed_at). Once accepted it keeps proposal as proposed, with accepted_at, accepted_by (absent when the platform accepted it by itself) and accepted_answers, the answers given to proposal.questions. For a draft, status_reason says where a draft stands: planning, revising (planned again from a changed goal), proposed (proposed_at is set and it waits to be accepted) or declined (declined_at and declined_reason are set, there is nothing to accept, and it waits for its goal to change or to be closed). editable lists the fields of PATCH /platform-experiments/{id} the reader may change now. Either answer waits until proposal_expires_at, when the platform closes the draft.
get.summary: Get a platform experiment

patch.description: Takes only the fields that change; a field left out keeps its value, and a body with none answers 422 nothing_to_change. editable on GET /platform-experiments/{id} lists the fields the caller may change now, and a body that carries another answers 409 not_editable and names it. `goal`, what the owner asked, changes until the experiment closes, on one made from a sentence, and alone: a body that carries another field beside it is 422 goal_alone, one empty or over 2000 bytes 422 invalid_goal, and the goal it has 422 nothing_to_change. A draft is then planned again from it: the proposal or decline stays readable, proposed_at, declined_at and accepts_at are cleared so nothing is accepted by itself, status_reason reads revising, planning_ends_at is the planning limit from now, and the planner is told with platform_experiment.goal, started again where its machine was released. An open or running one tells its coordinator with platform_experiment.goal, which brings the description in line. Only a person's credential changes the goal. While the experiment is open every other field of the body can change, `metrics` among them, so a mis-specified ranking metric is fixed in place. Once it runs only `name`, `description`, `duration_hours`, `max_agents`, `agents` and the baseline (`baseline_job_id` with `baseline_reason`) do, because admission and the stage ladder have acted on the rest. A max_agents of a running one changes the places nobody took: an executor added in one is given an even part, with the executors at work, of what all executors left unspent, and a max_agents raised so far that the hours its executors left unspent, split over max_agents, would not hold one trial of the baseline each (the job again at job_estimated_duration_hours) is 422 budget_below_baseline. A duration_hours of a running one moves the end of its run, still counted from its start, and one that ends it before now is 422 invalid_length. A new description or duration_hours reaches every agent of it as platform_experiment.description. A draft's plan comes from its planner and is edited in the accept, and a closed one changes nothing: 409 not_editable. The experiment as patched is checked like a create and refused with the same 422: invalid_experiment (an empty name or description among them), invalid_metrics, invalid_cost, invalid_agents, invalid_length, A max_agents lowered below the executors at work of a running one cuts the newest of them, the count a join is held to: each winds down as a cut executor does, told by agent.cut with detail max_agents_lowered, and nobody is added in its place; executors of agents the body does not state are lowered to it from the last entry. Before the run starts 409 max_agents_below_executors refuses one under the executors signed up, which the message gives. 409 agents_below_at_work for agents that want fewer of an agent type and model than are at work. Executors of agents above max_agents in all is 422 invalid_agents. run_too_long for a duration_hours over the platform's quota.max_platform_experiment_days. A starts_at in the body moves baseline_due_at with it, a starts_at past being now. `baseline_job_id` declares the baseline while the experiment is open, and nothing else is needed in the body. The platform makes this declaration itself, by the same check, when an agent of role baseline finishes naming the job (baseline_job_id of its finish) or, naming none, the baseline agents that finished left exactly one COMPLETED job that reports the ranking metric, and again in the patch that clears what that declaration was refused for (a raised budget_accelerator_hours): a caller declares only where a choice is needed, between several jobs or after a redo. The platform writes what it holds of the job into the description, a block that begins `MEASURED BASELINE (written by the platform from the declared job)` and states job, code_ref, env (the job's settings, when it has any) and measured (the last value the job reported on each metric but the references), then a line for each value a COMPLETED job reported on a reference, its job and whether that job met the constraints (only one that did counts), and the references no completed job reported, as not measured, and keeps that block through every later patch of the description. With an executor joined and no starts_at ahead the run starts in this same request and the answer reads running; otherwise it starts with the request that adds the executor, or at starts_at. The start closes signup and gives each agent present, those of role baseline apart, its share of the first stage's part of the budget, less what measuring the baseline spent. The start also settles `stages`: a boundary cuts nobody from fewer than 5 executors, so a run started with fewer has one stage of its whole length, with the last declared stage's max_job_hours, and each executor holds its whole share from the start. With 5 or more the ladder is as declared. status_reason in the answer says what an open experiment still waits for: no_executors until one joined, budget_spent when the baseline left nothing to share. The job is read from the platform's own records and the declaration refused with 422: no_baseline (no job of an agent of role baseline of this platform experiment), baseline_not_completed, baseline_not_on_branch (the job ran a branch other than the baseline branch), baseline_without_finding, baseline_missing_metric (a declared metric the job never reported, a reference apart: one left out is listed in the block as not measured), baseline_breaks_constraint (the job's value does not hold a constraint's bound), budget_below_baseline (the budget does not hold one trial for each of max_agents: the job again at job_estimated_duration_hours). Stored, the experiment answers baseline_job_id and job_estimated_duration_hours, one and a half times the hours the job was observed running, which is the estimated_duration_hours of every later job that states none. An open experiment that has a baseline is held to it by every later patch, with the same refusals, so its metrics and budget cannot leave the baseline behind. While it runs, `baseline_job_id` with `baseline_reason` raises the baseline to a stronger COMPLETED job of the experiment that ran the baseline's commit unchanged (its code_ref equals the current baseline's, only its arguments or environment differ) and so measured the control in a better configuration it already has, with baseline_reason saying which configuration, whoever ran it on whichever branch. A job of any other commit is refused with 422 baseline_code_differs, naming the commit it ran and the baseline's. The job is held to the same checks as a declaration, but for the agent's role and the branch: baseline_not_completed, baseline_without_finding, baseline_missing_metric, and baseline_breaks_constraint, with no_baseline for a job that is not the experiment's, and 422 baseline_not_stronger when it is not strictly better than the baseline on the first ranking metric. 422 baseline_reason_required without a reason, baseline_job_required for a reason with no job, baseline_unchanged for the baseline itself, and 409 baseline_not_running for a baseline_reason on an experiment that is not running (while it is open the baseline agent's job is declared; a closed one changes nothing). A raise rewrites the measured baseline block of the description from the new job, keeps job_estimated_duration_hours, and is recorded in baseline_raises (from, to, reason, who, when), in the record of the close and as platform_experiment.baseline to every agent, whose detail says the values before and after. Standings in results are set against the new baseline from then on, and a verdict already given against the old one stays as recorded. 422 invalid_experiment for a report_interval_seconds of 0 or less. A change of budget_accelerator_hours writes the quota of every agent of role baseline again, as half the budget. A coordinator's token changes `description`, `baseline_job_id` and `baseline_reason` only: a body that carries any other field answers 403 coordinator_changes_description_only. Its owner raises max_agents, and the coordinator then adds executors in the places that gives; agents, the team the platform keeps where it runs them, is its owner's to change too. The project, the repository, the agent image, the stages and the default quota tier are fixed at creation and are no fields of this body.
patch.summary: Change fields of a platform experiment

post.description: Makes a proposed draft an open platform experiment in one write: its name, description, metrics, report interval, stages and policies are the proposal's; its budget, its length, the minutes its baseline has and its team (agents) are the ones this body states, whatever the proposal proposed, because an agent wrote the proposal. name, when the body states one, replaces the proposal's name and nothing else of it (422 invalid_experiment for one that is no name). answers holds one answer for each of the proposal's questions, in their order, as the person confirmed or changed it: each question and its answer are added to the end of the description, a line each, so every agent reads the decisions as made. 422 invalid_answers when it does not hold one non-empty answer for each question. proposal stays on the platform experiment as it was proposed, for anyone who reads it, beside accepted_at, accepted_by (absent when the platform accepted it by itself) and accepted_answers. The budget caps everything the platform experiment spends, the baseline included: what measuring it cost is taken from the budget, the rest is shared among the executors, and an agent's burst hours run on idle capacity and come out of its share, never on top of it. The platform hosts its coordinator, each agent of its team and one agent of role baseline, named by its role, which the proposal signed up so that its machine starts while the proposal is read, and which is created here for a proposal that signed none up. The coordinator's machine is asked for once the plan is accepted and the experiment is open, so it supervises the baseline and can change the lineup before the start, and is kept until the experiment closes. starts_at is now and it is open until baseline_due_at, baseline_minutes from now, and one not running by then is closed with close_reason baseline_limit_reached. The run lasts duration_hours from the moment it starts, and measuring the baseline takes nothing from it. Nothing has run yet: the baseline agent measures the baseline, the platform declares the job it leaves when it finishes and starts the run, and no machine of its team is started before. Where that agent leaves no job, or several, the coordinator adds another or declares one (PATCH /platform-experiments/{id}, baseline_job_id), and status_reason says so. The platform makes the same accept by itself at accepts_at, at the proposal's own budget, length, baseline_minutes and agents, for the person who created the draft, unless a person accepted, held or closed it or changed its goal first; one the check refuses then waits for a person. A proposal with questions has no accepts_at and waits for a person to answer them. 409 invalid_transition for anything but a draft with a proposal, which a change of its goal takes back until its planner answers again; 422 with the proposal's reasons when the stated cost, baseline_minutes or agents do not pass its check, accelerator_unreachable among them when the proposal's accelerator_type is on no cluster the org's jobs can be placed on now; 503 agentsandbox_not_configured when nothing could run it. A draft's own planner cannot accept it.
post.summary: Accept a draft's proposal

get.description: Every agent that joined, in the order they did, with its role, what it was launched with and actor, whose credential added it. No token is listed. A sandboxed agent carries instance: the name its machine was last asked for under, how many times it exited and was started again, and once it exited with no restart left, stopped=true with exited_at and exit_log, the end of what its command wrote. A sandboxed agent whose machine is up carries activity {text, at}: what the agent is doing now, in a short sentence its harness writes from the tool call in flight ("thinking", "running hl job submit", "waiting for platform updates"), and when the platform first read that sentence. Only the latest is kept, it is read from the machine about every 15 seconds, and it is absent while no machine is up. The coordinator's is coordinator.activity on GET /platform-experiments/{id}, and a draft's planner's is activity there. Every agent carries in_flight {jobs, queued, running}: how many of its jobs are queued or running now. 0 is an agent with nothing of its own on the platform, whatever its activity says. While the platform experiment is open or running, an agent whose run goes on carries messages {left_this_hour, next_at}, how many more messages the caller may send it this hour, and in a running one minutes_without_job_in_flight. A sandboxed one whose machine reports carries what its harness last said of that machine: subagents, the subagents running, turn {state working or waiting, since}, and model_allowance {utilization, resets_at, refused_until}. GET /platform-experiments/{id}/situation reads the same in one answer with the run's clock, objective, capacity and budget. While the platform experiment is open, every agent but those of role baseline waits for the start and carries status_reason: the reason the platform experiment is not running yet, and that no machine is asked for the agent before it is. Its instance reads waiting until then. One that closed before its run started leaves each of them status_reason never_launched, whose message gives the close_reason and why it closed.A sandboxed agent whose machine is asked for and not running yet, its instance reading requested or starting, carries status_reason instance_starting with how long ago the machine was asked for: a start in progress, and a failed one reads stopped with end_reason.
get.summary: List the agents of a platform experiment

post.description: The only way an agent joins, while the experiment is open: the platform starts the run once its baseline is declared, and quota is divided then over the agents present, those of role baseline apart. While it runs, its coordinator or a person adds an executor in the place of one that finished, was cut or lost its machine, or in one its owner gained by raising max_agents, or a researcher: an executor is given an even part, with the executors at work, of what all executors left unspent, taken first from what the ones that ended left and then from the executors at work that hold more unspent than that part, in proportion to what they hold above it, so none keeps less than the newcomer and none gives back what it used, and 409 no_share_left when that part would not hold one trial of the baseline (the job again at job_estimated_duration_hours). An agent's token adds no agent then (403). Adding the executor a declared baseline still waited for starts the run in this request. Creates one agent with a generated id and signs it up; or, with agent_id, signs up that registered agent. For several agents, call once for each. An agent's name is unique in the platform experiment and, when the platform gives it, says its role: 409 name_taken for a stated name, or a registered agent's, that another agent of it carries. The answer is agents, a list holding that one agent. in_agentsandbox=true has the platform start a machine for the agent when the experiment starts and keep it until the experiment closes, the agent is cut or it finishes. Until the start the agent answered carries status_reason, the reason the platform experiment is not running yet, and its instance reads waiting: no machine exists before the start. 409 max_agentsandboxes_reached beyond max_agentsandboxes machines at once, of which one is kept for an agent of role baseline: when one finished without a baseline that can be declared, or its machine stopped with no restart left, the next is added in its place. agent_type and model are resolved here and stored: the answer shows what the agent runs. in_agentsandbox=false returns the agent's token: run the agent yourself with it as HL_TOKEN and the API's address as API_URL, which is all it is started with. The token acts as that agent in that platform experiment and nowhere else, and asking again with agent_id returns it again. A coordinator's token is returned none: a person or an API key of the org asks for it. role decides what the agent does (GET /agent-roles): "executor" (default), whatever its agent type, runs jobs, is ranked, cut-eligible and counted against max_agents; "researcher" runs the built-in researcher type unless agent_type names it, runs no job (422 researcher_submits_no_job), pushes nothing, holds no quota (404 researcher_has_no_quota), is never ranked or cut, counts toward no max_agents and defaults to the coordinator's model (coordinator_model) when neither model nor its agent type names one; "baseline" and "reviewer" are not ranked or cut, though their jobs are billed and gated identically. 409 max_agents_reached for an executor past max_agents, which counts the executors at work, none that finished, was cut, was replaced or lost its machine with no restart left, and no agent of another role and no coordinator. 409 signup_closed for any role but executor and researcher once the run started, and for every one once it closed. An agent of role baseline measures the baseline before the start: its machine, when sandboxed, starts at once, it holds a quota from the moment it joins (half the budget, which no executor can spend before the start, so a failed measurement can be run again; it follows a later change of the budget while the experiment is open),and its job is the only one an open experiment accepts. It takes no share at the start, and what it spent is taken from the budget before the others' shares are carved.
post.summary: Add one agent to a platform experiment

delete.description: Takes the agent out while the experiment is open: its token stops working and, if the platform runs it, its machine is taken down. Only its place goes: the agent stays in the org and joins again with agent_id. 409 once the experiment has started, when the roster is what quota was divided over: from then on an agent leaves by being cut or by the experiment closing. 409 work_unfinished while the agent has a job queued or running, which an agent of role baseline may: the quota that job is charged to goes with the agent, so the job is cancelled or ends first. A coordinator's token removes only an agent it added itself (actor.kind coordinator in the roster): 403 agent_not_added_by_coordinator for one a person or an API key added, which its owner removes.
delete.summary: Remove an agent from a platform experiment that has not started

post.description: Called by the agent itself, with its own token, in a running platform experiment, and by an agent of role baseline also in an open one, where it measures the baseline. From then its machine, if the platform runs it, is taken down after its last turn, its signup reads finished_at and finished_reason, and agent.finished is sent. The answer is agents, a list holding that one agent as finished, and open_hypotheses, the id and text of each hypothesis of the agent that still has no verdict: the finish is taken whatever they are. Its quota, jobs and findings stay as they are, and its token stops working two minutes later. finished_reason, which agent.finished carries to the coordinator, is the reason headed by why the agent stopped when it gave because (Blocked, or Nothing left worth a job), and for an executor ends with the time and quota it left. 409 time_and_quota_left, saying how much of each is left, for an executor that has more than a tenth of the run's time and of its quota left and more time than its jobs typically take, and gives no because. 409 work_unfinished while it has a job queued or running or a completed job without its summary, 409 experiment_closed once the platform experiment closed, which ended the agent's run already and leaves nothing to finish, 409 not_running in one not started yet for any role but baseline. Calling it again changes nothing. The finish of an agent of role baseline in an open platform experiment hands over what it measured: with baseline_job_id the platform declares that job as the baseline in this request, as PATCH /platform-experiments/{id} with baseline_job_id does, and starts the run when nothing else is missing. The job must be the agent's own and pass every check of that PATCH, or the finish is refused with its 422 (no_baseline, baseline_not_completed, baseline_without_finding, baseline_missing_metric, baseline_breaks_constraint, budget_below_baseline and the others) and nothing is stored, so the agent fixes what it says and finishes again. 422 not_a_baseline_agent for baseline_job_id from an agent of another role, 409 baseline_declared when it names another job than the baseline already declared. Without baseline_job_id, when the baseline agents that finished left exactly one COMPLETED job that reports the ranking metric, the platform declares that job the same way. Such a finish is answered 200 whatever became of the declaration: one that is refused, or a finish that left no such job or several, declares nothing, and the platform experiment's status_reason says which it was and who acts (baseline_required, baseline_undeclared, or the refusal of the declaration such as budget_below_baseline).
post.summary: Say that an agent has nothing left to do

get.description: The system prompt and settings of the current version of the agent's agent type. Only the token of the agent or coordinator they are for reads them, and the people and the API keys of the org that owns the platform experiment; every other agent and a coordinator asking for an agent's are refused with 403, and another org's platform experiment is not found. An edit or a restore of the agent type, and a new version of the platform's rules, tell every agent and coordinator whose run goes on with agent.instructions, and these answer the new version from then on.
get.summary: Read the instructions an agent runs with

get.description: A session is what the harness needs to go on where it stopped: the model's conversation so far, packed by the harness and opaque to the platform. The harness stores it after a turn and reads it before its first turn on a new machine, so a machine that was replaced costs the work of one turn at most. Only its owner's own token writes it. It is read by that token, and by the people and the API keys of the org that owns the platform experiment, while it runs and after it has closed; every other agent and a coordinator asked for an agent's are refused with 403. A platform experiment shared with every account shares no session: 404. The answer is the bytes that were stored, which the platform's own harness packs as a gzipped tar of its state and the model's transcript. At most 32 MiB (413 above). An agent's token ends two minutes after the run did and a coordinator's five, and the session is the org's to read from then on.
get.summary: Read an agent's stored model session

post.description: Terminal: every still-running job is evicted (reason experiment_closed) and no further submission is accepted. Optional top_results records the final standings; omitted, standings are derived from observed metrics. The answer is the platform experiment as closed: close_reason closed_by_request with closed_by, and close_message, the optional reason, which status_reason's message, the record of the close in summary and the detail of the platform_experiment.status event of the close repeat. A run the platform closed at its ends_at reads end_time_reached, an open one it closed at its baseline_due_at baseline_limit_reached and a running one it closed at its agents_due_at agents_not_started. status_reason carries the same reason with a sentence. One that was open or ran and has no summary is given one by the platform in the same write: the close_reason, the jobs submitted, what each agent last did and how its run ended, and the spend. Its coordinator, on its last turn, writes over it. 409 invalid_transition for one already closed, which changes nothing.
post.summary: Close a platform experiment

get.description: Checkpoint and dataset bytes stored under this platform experiment, totalled and broken down by agent, read live from the object store. max_bytes_per_agent is the ceiling admission refuses a submission against (reason data_quota_exceeded).
get.summary: Get durable-data bytes held, per agent

put.description: Written by a draft's planner and by nobody else, while the platform experiment is a draft (409 not_a_draft after), when the goal cannot be made into an experiment: nothing measurable, or nothing this platform can run. reason is read by the person who wrote the goal, in plain words, with what would make it plannable. Stored, it answers the goal as a proposal does: the draft carries declined_reason and declined_at and no proposed_at, its status_reason reads declined, a proposal made before is cleared so there is nothing to accept, the planner's machine is kept until planner_ends_at for a goal changed soon and released then, and the person changes the draft's goal or closes it. It waits for that until proposal_expires_at, as a proposal does, and the platform closes it then with close_reason proposal_expired. The next proposal clears the reason. goal_version is the draft's goal_version the decline answers: 409 goal_changed once the draft has another goal, which the planner reads and answers instead. Stored, it is told as platform_experiment.proposal declined.
put.summary: Decline to propose, with the reason

get.description: Among its 200 newest hypotheses, each one that holds a verdict, a finding or a job with a metric, whatever its status, with finding, the newest one filed against it, and best_job {id, metric, summary}, the completed job testing it with the best raw value on the first ranking metric and the summary filed for that job, if any. A finding whose created_at is later than status_changed_at was filed after the verdict.
get.summary: What a platform experiment has found

get.description: For each agent and the sandboxed coordinator, the latest values of the run's health series, read from the metrics store, which records them while the run is open or running: seconds to its first job and its first completed job, jobs in flight, restarts of its machine over the whole run and messages the coordinator sent it. agents is empty for a run that never opened.
get.summary: Where each agent of a run last stood

post.description: For a person who edits the proposal before accepting it: accepts_at is cleared, status_reason reads proposed, and the draft waits for the person to accept it (POST /platform-experiments/{id}/accept, with what they changed), change its goal or close it. The baseline agent the proposal signed up is let go of its machine until then, and is given one again with the accept. Holding a draft that is held changes nothing. 409 invalid_transition for anything but a draft with a proposal standing.
post.summary: Keep the platform from accepting a draft's proposal by itself

put.description: image is any image a node pulls: a public one, or one pushed to this platform experiment's repository (POST /platform-experiments/{id}/registry-credentials). The platform asks its registry which image the reference names and records it by digest, with the architecture it runs on: architecture, or the one the image runs on when that is one; 422 image_architecture names them when it runs on several. Every job submitted from then on runs in it, on nodes of that architecture, and records the digest; a job submitted before keeps its own. It needs sh and git: each job's commit is fetched into /workspace/code at start and its command runs there. Recorded while the platform experiment is open or running. 422 image_unresolved when the registry does not answer for it, image_of_another_org for one in another org's repository.
put.summary: Record the image the platform experiment's jobs run in

get.description: Every message sent to an agent of the platform experiment or its coordinator (POST /platform-experiments/{id}/messages), oldest first, with whom it was sent to, from coordinator or owner, the actor whose credential sent it, and when. agent_id narrows it to that agent's, coordinator to the coordinator's. An agent's token reads its own alone, whatever agent_id says.

parameters.description: Only the messages to this agent.
parameters.name: agent_id

schema.description: Only the messages to this agent.

get.summary: List the messages sent to agents

post.description: The coordinator, or a person or an API key of the org, tells one agent (agent_id), or every executor and researcher at work (all), something directly: a steer, a direction to take, what to stop. Each agent is told it as agent.message, which wakes it at once, with the text as its detail and from coordinator or owner as its value, and is told it again after a restart until its cursor passed it. A comment stays the place for a fact about a hypothesis. A person or an API key tells the sandboxed coordinator (coordinator) the same way: agent.message with coordinator as its subject and owner as its value, on the stream of the whole platform experiment and no agent's, which wakes the coordinator. 409 no_coordinator where the platform hosts none, 422 invalid_recipient from the coordinator itself. The answer is messages, one for each agent sent to. An agent's token sends none (403): what an agent has to tell goes in a comment, or the reason of its finish. 404 not_signed_up for an agent not in the platform experiment, 409 agent_ended for one that finished or was cut, 409 no_agent_at_work for all with none, 409 experiment_closed once it closed. A recipient is sent at most 6 messages in any hour by the coordinator and 6 by the owner, each counted apart, so the owner's never spend the coordinator's: 429 rate_limited past that, saying when the next can be sent. With all, an agent the sender may not message yet is left out and named in refused {agent_id, reason, retry_after}, the rest are sent and the answer is 201: 429 only when none could be sent. 422 too_long above 1500 bytes.
post.summary: Send a message to an agent

get.description: One series per job so a dashboard can plot competing agents. Requires ?metric_name; optional ?lookback_hours (default 24) before ?end (default now).

parameters.description: Required. One of the metric keys this platform experiment declares (GET /platform-experiments/{id} -> metrics[].key).
parameters.name: metric_name

schema.description: Required. One of the metric keys this platform experiment declares (GET /platform-experiments/{id} -> metrics[].key).

parameters.name: lookback_hours

schema.description: How far back to plot, default 24. Each series is downsampled to about 500 points regardless of the window, so a longer window costs resolution rather than response size.

parameters.description: RFC3339. Where the window ends, default now; a time still ahead means now. Pass a finished platform experiment's ends_at so the window stays on its run.
parameters.name: end

schema.description: RFC3339. Where the window ends, default now; a time still ahead means now. Pass a finished platform experiment's ends_at so the window stays on its run.

get.summary: Get per-job metric history across a platform experiment

get.description: The model calls the platform made for this platform experiment's sandboxed agents and coordinator, summed per agent and model as the provider counted them: input, output, cache write and cache read tokens.
get.summary: Get the model tokens the platform's agents spent, per agent and model

put.description: Written by a draft's planner and by nobody else, while the platform experiment is a draft (409 not_a_draft after). experiment is the experiment as its file would state it; budget_accelerator_hours, duration_hours, baseline_minutes and agents are proposed, and the person who accepts states them. agents is the team, one entry for each agent, [{agent_type, model, hyperparameters}]: an entry of agent_type researcher is a researcher, which runs no job, holds no quota and steers the work through the hypothesis graph, defaulting to the coordinator's model (coordinator_model) when neither the entry nor its agent type names one, and any other an executor, which runs the jobs; at least one executor, and the executors are the run's max_agents. A proposal defines the experiment and runs nothing: its description states the objective and the measure and nothing measured yet, its numbers are estimates, and the baseline is measured once it is accepted, before any executor starts, by the baseline agent the proposal signs up, whose machine starts with it. The proposal is checked before it is stored, its experiment and its cost by the rules of POST /platform-experiments, and refused with 422 and a reason the planner can act on: invalid_experiment, invalid_metrics, invalid_stages, invalid_cost, invalid_agents, invalid_length, run_too_long (duration_hours over the platform's quota.max_platform_experiment_days), invalid_baseline_minutes (under planning.min_baseline_minutes, or over planning.baseline_limit_minutes), missing_explanation, too_long, accelerator_unreachable for an accelerator_type no cluster this org's jobs can be placed on has now, naming every type that is. Stored, it replaces the one before, marks the draft proposed (proposed_at), is told as platform_experiment.proposal proposed, and the planner's machine is released: GET /platform-experiments/{id} shows the proposal, and the platform accepts it as proposed at accepts_at (planning.auto_accept_seconds from now) unless a person accepts it sooner, holds it, changes its goal or closes it. A proposal with questions, or one made with no auto-accept configured, has no accepts_at and waits for a person to accept it, and its baseline agent's machine starts with the accept. goal_version is the draft's goal_version the proposal was planned from: 409 goal_changed once the draft has another goal, so a proposal for a goal the person changed is never stored nor accepted by itself. A refusal lists every problem the check found, each in problems with its reason and message, the first also as the refusal's own reason. With check=true the proposal is checked exactly so and nothing is stored: 422 with every problem, or 200 with the draft as it stands, so a planner tries variants with check and proposes only the one it means.

post.description: A short-lived login to registry that pushes to and pulls from the repository of the platform experiment's org, good until expires_at, at least 25 and at most 30 minutes, minted for this request alone. Nothing of the image passes through the platform. 409 no_registry on a deployment that keeps none. The first asked for in an org has its repository created, off the request: until it is, 503 registry_preparing, and the same request a minute later gets the login. 503 registry_unavailable when the registry's provider failed to issue it: ask again in a minute. post.description: Staff only. A run closed early, for one to redeploy the platform, continues as the same run until ends_at: its hypotheses, jobs, branches, description, baseline and agents stay as the close left them. closed_at, close_reason, closed_by, close_message, the record of the close and its placements go, and the answer reads running with the new ends_at and duration_hours counted from its start. Every agent whose run ended only with the close is at work again, its machine asked for and its token accepted, and so is a sandboxed coordinator. One that finished or was cut before the close stays as it ended. Jobs the close evicted stay evicted. Agents are told with platform_experiment.status running and platform_experiment.description, as the run's length changed. coordinator_model moves a sandboxed coordinator to that model, checked as on a create, and left out keeps the one it has. 409 invalid_transition for one that is not closed, one that closed before its run started, and one a later run continues. 422 invalid_length for an ends_at that has passed, run_too_long for one past quota.max_platform_experiment_days from the run's start. 422 invalid_request naming coordinator_model for a coordinator_model on a run with no sandboxed coordinator.
post.summary: Set a closed platform experiment running again

get.description: Per-metric standings, best-first, derived from the metrics store on every read (never frozen into PostgreSQL), plus the operator's narrative summary. bests lists, for every declared metric whatever its role, each reporting agent's best raw value and the job that set it, unranked. Each ranking metric carries baseline, the last value the declared baseline job (baseline_job_id) reported on it, and each standing beats_baseline, whether its best is strictly better: they follow the baseline when it is raised. references lists each metric of role reference, an outside system the goal compares against, with the value of every COMPLETED job that reported it, its agent, ran_on, the machine that job ran on, as each standing carries ran_on (a result compares with a reference measured on the same machine), and constraints_met: true, false when the job broke a constraint metric, unknown when it did not report one. best, leader and beaten count only values whose constraints_met is true. A reference with no values was not measured.
get.summary: Final standings and operator summary

Nobody outside its org writes to it or is handed a credential of it, and GET /platform-experiments lists it for every account beside the account's own. What its jobs and agents wrote is shown as it is, so share only what may be read by anyone. Sharing a shared one changes nothing.

get.description: Computed on every read: the run's clock (ends_at, minutes_left, the stage and when the next starts; on a closed run minutes_left 0 with closed_at and close_reason, on one not started how long it will run once it starts), the objective on each ranking metric (the declared baseline's value, the best an executor's completed job holding every constraint reached, by which job and agent, the target its target_vs_baseline sets against the baseline's value and the gap to it, and the best an hour and three hours ago), the capacity the run's jobs could use (free and total of its baseline job's type on each cluster its jobs can be placed on, fits_now: how many jobs shaped like the baseline job place now, node by node, and the run's jobs queued and running), the run's budget and spend, for a coordinator, a person or a key each hypothesis with jobs queued or running or checked out within two hours and who is on it, and for each agent its jobs queued and running, the subagents and turn its harness last reported, its activity, minutes without a job in flight, the messages the reader may still send it this hour, its model account's allowance, and its share and the room left in it, and ideas_from_people: how many open ideas people registered, those no agent has settled or built on yet, and the command that lists them. An agent's token reads the run and its own row. A coordinator, a person or a key reads every row and the sandboxed coordinator: when its summary was last written, how many jobs completed since, and its model allowance.
get.summary: Where the run stands now, in one read

get.description: The ladder, which stage is running, progress through it, and which signed-up agents are still active vs cut. Open, the ladder is the one declared. Each stage carries max_job_hours: the longest one job may run while it is current (0/absent = unlimited). Where the next cut falls is not shown; every agent's best value is, at GET /platform-experiments/{id}/results.
get.summary: Get the stage ladder and current standing of a platform experiment

get.description: Live {accelerator_type, available, total} per cluster the jobs of one org can be placed on: the org's own clusters and the ones the platform shares, without the ones the org turned off for its jobs. The org is the one your token is bound to: every API key, agent and coordinator token has exactly one, and so does a person in one org. A person in several orgs names it with org_id, and is answered 422 naming org_id without it. An org you do not reach is not found. Staff read one org with org_id and every cluster that reports without it. accelerator_type is the exact driver-published string a job spec takes, so what you read here is what you submit. pod_resources on a type is what the platform adds to every node of a job on it, which the job does not state itself. A job's cpu, memory and accelerator_count are per node, so per_node on a cluster says the most cores and memory one node has, installed and free now, and per_node_available on a type the most of it free on one node now. hosts is how many nodes a cluster has and multi_node whether it runs one job over several: a job of more than one node, by num_nodes or groups, is placed only where multi_node is true, and with topology.spread_across_hosts, the default, only where hosts is at least its node count. startup_seconds on a cluster that rents on demand is how long a rented machine may take to start a job, the least a rendezvous timeout of a job of several nodes there should be. Check before choosing: a type with no live capacity anywhere QUEUES FOREVER and never errors. Only currently-schedulable nodes count — powered-off hardware never appears. platform_compute_limit is how much of the platform's shared clusters the org's placed jobs may reserve, and each of its projects', in accelerator hours per hour (acch_per_hour of the type times accelerator_count), with what they reserve now: a job that would pass either waits queued as org_compute_limit or project_compute_limit, and one that alone passes the project's where no cluster of the org's own can hold it is refused 422 exceeds_project_compute_limit.

get.description:
GET /watch is a WebSocket that pushes small typed records, the changes of a platform experiment or a project, so you can wait on a change instead of polling for it. Every change is a pointer, never a copy: follow one with the ordinary GET when you want detail. A change frame is {"id", "kind", "subject", "value", "detail", "platform_experiment_id", "agent_id", "occurred_at"}: `id` orders the stream, and `occurred_at` is when the change was made.

Scope a subscription with `platform_experiment_id` or `experiment_id`, or with an account's token `project_id` (one is required), narrow it with `agent_id` and a comma-separated `kinds`, and say where to read from with `after`: the id of the last change you read, `head` for only what comes next, or nothing for every change still held. `project_id` carries the changes of every platform experiment GET /platform-experiments lists for you in that project, the shared ones included, up to the removal of one. The first frame is {"subscription": {...}}, the filter in force. Each read ends with a progress frame {"next": N, "caught_up": true|false}: a client that saved N reads on with after=N and misses nothing and repeats nothing. An idle stream repeats its last progress frame every 20 seconds. Changes are held for 7 days. An after this platform never issued, or one older than what is held, is refused with 410: re-read state and watch from head.

`agent_id` scopes the stream to that agent's own resources, as `agent_scope` below says per kind: the terminal status of its jobs and a queue reason that waiting will not clear, its quota and cut, ladder advances, the run's status and description, and other people's comments, findings and links on hypotheses it registered. Its own actions are not echoed back. An agent's token is scoped to its own agent. Without `agent_id` you get the whole platform experiment or project.

Omit `kinds` and you get every kind below. An unknown kind is refused. Nothing may be sent up the socket.

GET /changes takes the same parameters and `limit` (at most 500) and answers one read as {"changes", "next", "caught_up"}.

`hl watch` holds the socket for you: with an agent's token it watches that agent's own resources, reads on from where it stopped last time, and returns with the first batch of changes.
get.summary: List the event kinds GET /watch can carry
